Finally, a GCN-based motion decoder is employed to synthesize physically plausible and semantically consistent motions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EgoHMP achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CRIL-U-Net: Compact Ratio-Interaction Learning for Focal Cortical Dysplasia Segmentation from T1w and FLAIR MRI
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) type II is an important cause of drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its small size and subtle magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) appearance make automated segmentation difficult. Conventional multimodal networks concatenate T1-weighted (T1w) and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images and rely on subsequent layers to learn their relationships implicitly. We propose Compact Ratio-Interaction Learning U-Net (CRIL-U-Net), a 3D U-Net extension incorporating a Compact Ratio-Interaction Learning module that combines local spatial features, voxel-wise cross-modal mixing, and bidirectional ratio-inspired interactions. CRIL-U-Net was compared with a 3D U-Net and a U-Net with input-level self-attention using five-fold cross-validation on 85 FCD subjects and 25 healthy controls. Each architecture was trained independently with Dice-binary cross-entropy (Dice-BCE) and Focal Tversky-Focal (FTF) losses. With FTF, CRIL-U-Net achieved the highest mean Dice score ($0.196\pm0.262$), compared with $0.136\pm0.224$ for the U-Net and $0.135\pm0.214$ for the attention comparator. It localised 44 of 85 lesions, compared with 36 for the U-Net, and significantly outperformed both comparison architectures after false-discovery-rate correction. CRIL adds only 4,320 parameters to the backbone, indicating that compact cross-modal representation learning can improve FCD segmentation when combined with an imbalance-aware objective. The remaining 48.2\% miss rate nevertheless requires further methodological development and external validation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Gene Expression from H&E using Pathology Foundation Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Predicting gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images offers a scalable and cost-effective approach to deriving spatial molecular insights from routine histology. Pathology foundation models, typically pretrained using tile-level objectives, may not adequately capture the fine-grained cellular features required for single-cell molecular prediction. In this work, we systematically evaluate and establish domain-informed and task-specific strategies for adapting pathology foundation models to single-cell spatial gene expression prediction. Using paired H&E and Xenium 5K data, our approach improves mean gene-wise Pearson correlation by 2.67x over the standard zero-shot baseline and achieves state-of-the-art performance on this task. We demonstrate strong gene-detection performance across the full gene panel (AUROC = 0.800) and importantly identify that predictive performance varies substantially across biological contexts, with our model achieving its highest Pearson correlation for spatially variable genes (r = 0.643). Our findings demonstrate that, despite the challenges of sparse single-cell measurements, H&E-derived representations can recover biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns, highlighting both the opportunities and limitations of morphology-based molecular inference at cellular resolution.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI at Scale for Clinical Impact. Project page: https://he2sc-st.github.io/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Aligning Forest and Trees in Images & Long Captions for Visually Grounded Understanding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-language models such as CLIP often struggle to faithfully understand long, detail-rich captions, relying on dominant scene cues while overlooking fine-grained visual evidence. We propose a hierarchical vision-language learning principle for understanding scenes as part-to-whole compositions: before forming a whole-scene representation, a model should uncover what semantic parts appear where in the image. To this end, we propose CAFT (Cross-domain Alignment of Forest and Trees), a vision-language model that jointly learns local text-region alignment at intermediate representations and global image-text alignment at the final representation. Exploiting the organization of long captions, where local descriptions often correspond to scene parts, CAFT employs a fine-to-coarse image encoder and a part-whole text encoder to discover localized part semantics and progressively compose them into a global image-text representation. Trained on 30M image-text pairs, CAFT achieves state-of-the-art performance on six long-text retrieval benchmarks and exhibits strong scaling behavior. Experiments show that CAFT learns fine-grained representations that localize textual semantics in image regions without explicit region-level supervision.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://byeongju.me/CAFT

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: picoEmergencyNet : Attention-Enhanced Ultra-Small Deep Learning Model for Aerial Image Classification in Emergency Monitoring
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Real-time disaster recognition from aerial imagery requires deep learning models that operate under strict memory, compute, and latency constraints. While recent approaches achieve high accuracy, their computational cost limits deployment on resource-constrained UAV platforms. This work introduces picoEmergencyNet, an ultra-lightweight convolutional neural network designed for aerial image disaster classification. The proposed architecture combines depthwise dilated convolutions with efficient channel attention and channel shuffling to enable multi-scale feature extraction at minimal computational cost. picoEmergencyNet has 23k parameters and 7M FLOPs, requiring only 0.1 MB of model storage. Evaluated on the AIDER and AIDERv2 disaster datasets, it achieves up to 96.1% accuracy, matching or exceeding state-of-the-art lightweight models that are orders of magnitude larger. Deployment experiments on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin show that, without hardware-specific optimizations, picoEmergencyNet achieves 258 FPS on GPU and 46 FPS on CPU with a 7x lower activation memory footprint compared to competing models. These results demonstrate that careful architectural specialization, rather than model scaling, enables highly efficient and accurate TinyML-ready disaster recognition for real-time UAV-based emergency monitoring.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 6 pages, Appeared in IJCNN2026 C. Kyrkou, "picoEmergencyNet: Attention-Enhanced Ultra-Small Deep Learning Model for Aerial Image Classification in Emergency Monitoring," 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN), Maastricht, Netherlands, 2026, pp. 1-6

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DepthGS: Depth-Guided Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Regularization for High-Quality Surface Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as an efficient representation for novel view synthesis, offering fast differentiable rendering and high visual fidelity, and has increasingly been extended to surface reconstruction. However, the relationship between depth information and reconstruction error remains insufficiently explored, limiting the principled design of geometric optimization strategies. To fill the above gap, we propose DepthGS, a depth-guided Gaussian splatting framework. We derive theoretical relations between depth discrepancies and reconstruction error under single-view and multi-view settings, and rigorously establish corresponding upper bounds on reconstruction error. The above analysis informs the design of adaptive regularization strategies in both single-view and multi-view optimization. More specifically, for single-view optimization, we propose a depth-difference-guided adaptive normal regularization strategy that modulates the normal constraint strength using a geometric reliability weight computed from local depth differences. For multi-view optimization, we introduce a cross-view depth consistency regularization strategy that promotes consistency between neighboring-view depth maps and the corresponding depth predictions obtained by transforming the current view's depth predictions into those neighboring views. Extensive experiments on DTU, Mip-NeRF360, and Tanks and Temples demonstrate that DepthGS achieves competitive performance in both surface reconstruction and novel view synthesis.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: To appear in IEEE Trans. on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: iCATS: Fast Video Generation via Interaction-Aware Sparse Attention and Timestep-Adaptive Sparsity
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Training-free sparse attention offers a practical acceleration solution to Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) via reducing computations without fine-tuning. It typically involves estimating the importance of query-key regions and deriving sparse masks to compute only the important candidates, which inevitably introduces approximation errors that may degrade generation quality. To better balance the efficiency-quality trade-off, we propose iCATS, integrating improved importance estimation and sparse mask construction with an efficient hardware execution strategy. Specifically, for importance estimation, unlike previous works that perform independent clustering over query and key tokens based on feature similarity to estimate attention scores, iCATS demonstrates that clustering based on query-key dot-product interactions is more accurate and further reformulates this objective as a simple quadratic form for low-cost computation. For sparse mask construction, instead of using a fixed top-p rule, we observe that tolerance to sparse approximation errors varies across denoising timesteps and therefore introduce an SNR-guided sparsity schedule to adjust sparsity dynamically, leading to higher accuracy. Finally, for hardware execution, we devise a tail-merging strategy to reduce padding overhead caused by irregular cluster sizes, improving GPU kernel utilization. Extensive experiments show that iCATS achieves $2.03\times$ acceleration with 31.017 dB PSNR on HunyuanVideo-T2V-13B and $1.55\times$ acceleration with 29.301 dB PSNR on Wan2.1-T2V-14B, delivering a state-of-the-art efficiency-quality trade-off.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FlashMotion: Ultra-Fast Long-Term 3D Motion Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D human motion generation plays a crucial role in game development, extended reality (XR), digital humans, and embodied simulation. Beyond motion generation, practical pipelines include rigging, retargeting, and rendering, making ultra-fast long-term 3D motion generation without compromising quality valuable for real-time interactive applications. Despite promising progress, high-quality long-horizon motion generation under tight inference budgets remains challenging, owing to 2 coupled bottlenecks: (1) generative strategies that require many sampling steps for high-quality 3D motion generation and (2) model architectures with substantial per-step computational and memory costs for long sequences. We present FlashMotion, a co-designed framework for high-quality long-horizon 3D motion generation under a strict inference budget, covering text-to-motion, music-to-dance, and speech-to-gesture tasks. To enhance trajectory-level efficiency, we introduce a 3D motion-space MeanFlow formulation with kinematic and dynamic consistency constraints for few-step generation, together with an Adaptive Soft masking mechanism for temporally coherent motion editing. To improve per-step efficiency, we design a lightweight non-autoregressive BiMamba architecture with condition-guided state selection and AdaIN-based condition fusion mechanism, enhancing cross-modal alignment and generalization to longer motion sequences. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FlashMotion achieves overall state-of-the-art performance in both quality and efficiency across text-to-motion, speech-to-gesture, and music-to-dance generation. Code is available at FlashMotion (https://github.com/Sun-Happy-YKX/FlashMotion).

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PUMA: Probability-Constrained Sequential Interaction for Forensic Localization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image manipulation localization must jointly exploit semantic structure and noise-sensitive forensic evidence. However, the effects of spatial correspondence, matching quality, and interaction order are often conflated. Existing semantic-forensic fusion methods provide complementary representations, but do not explicitly preserve quality-mismatch information during spatial correspondence or adaptively select the order in which information is propagated across branches. We propose PUMA (Probability-constrained Unbalanced Matching and Aggregation), which combines spatially constrained unbalanced optimal transport with position-wise convex selection between two sequential operators through a shared positional interface. Before normalization, PUMA retains signed transport-mass residuals, constructs row-stochastic cross-branch and within-noise-branch operators, and updates noise features through a gated residual path. PUMA achieves strong localization results on four test sets, with scores on COVERAGE and NIST16 exceeding the published results of the representative methods listed in our comparison. The experiments support the utility of local matching states and adaptive sequential interaction for cross-source localization and several post-processing conditions.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: When to Start Denoising? Adaptive Denoising Entry for Generative Video Compression
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Generative video compression offers a promising solution for compressing and reconstructing videos under extremely low bitrate constraints, among which the diffusion-based solutions still achieve the best performance by providing the powerful generative latent prior. However, their effectiveness critically depends on when the compressed latent is introduced into the diffusion process, which directly governs the trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and perceptual realism. To address this limitation, we identify denoising start-timestep selection as a key factor governing this trade-off and formulate it as a geometric optimization problem. Based on this formulation, we propose a novel adaptive diffusion entry method for generative video compression (ADE-GVC), the first timestep-aware generative video compression framework, featuring a lightweight predictor that estimates an adaptive denoising start point from the compressed latent. A temporal adapter further extracts compression-aware conditions and injects them into a pretrained video diffusion model, enabling the reconstruction of videos with both high fidelity and realism. More importantly, we observe a strong quantitative relationship between the predicted timesteps and the distortion between the original and compressed latents, providing empirical support for our optimization formulation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ADE-GVC achieves the state-of-the-art performance on perceptual metrics and substantially improves reconstruction realism over existing generative video compression methods. Notably, our ADE-GVC achieves an average bitrate savings of 40.99\% (on DISTS) and 95.24\% (on PSNR) compared to the latest open-source baseline GLC-Video.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Direct Trajectory Optimization for Inference-Time Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Alignment of text-to-image diffusion models with reward functions is a key challenge in controllable generation. Existing approaches typically rely on optimizing model inputs or fine-tuning denoising networks, which requires computationally expensive backpropagation through large denoising models. In this work, we propose Direct Trajectory Optimization (DTO), a training-free framework that performs alignment by directly optimizing the sampling trajectory of diffusion models. Specifically, DTO treats intermediate denoising scores and sampled noise as the optimization variables, eliminating the need for gradients through the denoising network. To mitigate the out-of-distribution problem, we introduce Reward-Optimized Score Guidance, which interpolates between the optimized scores and the pretrained model predictions to stabilize sampling, while providing a provable theoretical guarantee of reward improvement under constrained distributions. Empirically, DTO improves alignment performance across three diffusion models on two benchmarks, outperforming existing inference-time alignment methods while maintaining high efficiency. These results suggest that trajectory-level optimization is a promising direction for efficient and effective diffusion model alignment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Post-OCR Correction of Mixed-Script Uzbek Text: Byte-Level ByT5 with an Empirical Homoglyph Noise Matrix
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In Uzbek official and technical documents, a large share of OCR errors is caused not by poor image quality but by characters that are visually identical across the two alphabets in use. Because the script transition is still under way, Cyrillic and Latin appear on the same page and often within a single sentence, and in our measurements the density of homoglyph errors on such pages is close to five times higher than in single-script text. We study this problem in a setting where the corpus of engineering-geological and ICT infrastructure reports may not leave the organisation, so every stage was executed on local hardware. The proposed system combines a byte-level ByT5 model with a noise generator whose sampling weights are estimated from 359 manually classified error events, together with a Levenshtein-bounded conservative decoding rule. On a Gold set of 5,204 line pairs it lowers the character error rate from 0.0578 to 0.0369, restores 91.3% of the homoglyphs and introduces only 84 new errors.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the 10th International Conference on Future Networks and Distributed Systems (ICFNDS 2026), ACM ICPS. Code: https://github.com/OybekNarzullaev/byt5-uzbek-postocr

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LucidNFT: LR-Anchored Multi-Reward Preference Optimization for Flow-Based Real-World Super-Resolution
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Generative real-world image super-resolution (Real-ISR) can synthesize visually convincing details from severely degraded low-resolution (LR) inputs, but stochastic sampling can introduce semantic or structural hallucinations unsupported by the LR evidence. Sampling multiple outputs per LR input exposes trade-offs between perceptual quality and faithfulness that reinforcement learning (RL) can optimize beyond paired supervision. Effective alignment is limited by the lack of a degradation-robust LR-referenced faithfulness signal, the loss of per-objective reward contrasts when rewards are combined before normalization in Diffusion Negative-aware FineTuning (DiffusionNFT), and limited coverage of real degradations. We propose LucidNFT, a multi-reward RL framework for flow-matching Real-ISR. LucidNFT introduces LucidConsistency, a degradation-invariant LR-referenced evaluator trained with content-consistent degradation pools and hard negatives created by inpainting to detect localized hallucinations. Its decoupled reward normalization strategy normalizes each reward within each LR-conditioned rollout group before fusion, preserving per-objective contrasts across candidates. LucidLR provides a large-scale collection of real-world degraded images for RL fine-tuning. Experiments show that LucidNFT improves perceptual quality on strong flow-based Real-ISR baselines while generally maintaining LR-referenced consistency across diverse real-world scenarios. In a reward-independent human study, LucidNFT outputs were judged more faithful to the LR inputs in 72.5 percent of comparisons.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: When to Trust Adaptation: Contextual Fusion for Transferable Vision-Language Prompting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: When a vision-language model encounters a new class or domain, how much should it trust its learned prompts? Because source adaptation can correct pretrained errors on some target images while disturbing valid predictions on others, we introduce Contextual Adaptive Fusion (CAF), which retains four prediction branches by pairing frozen and prompted visual and textual representations. To arbitrate when branches disagree on an image, CAF combines each branch's predictive confidence with how frequently the branches favor its proposed class across the unlabeled target collection, placing greater trust in predictions that are locally confident yet less dominated by collection-wide frequency bias. The fusion coefficients are learned once on source data and remain fixed at inference. Trained on ImageNet, CAF achieves 69.96% average accuracy across ten cross-dataset benchmarks (1.92 percentage points above ManiPT) and remains highly competitive across four ImageNet variants, setting a new best of 52.21% on ImageNet-S. In base-to-novel transfer across eleven datasets, CAF further reaches 79.77% novel-class accuracy and an 82.81% harmonic mean. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyuanchenai/CAF.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GRACE: Adaptive Concept Erasure with Geometry-Guided Retention in Diffusion Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models inevitably internalize sensitive or non-compliant concepts from large-scale pretraining data, necessitating post-hoc concept erasure. However, existing erasure methods often lack explicit constraints on parameter updates, leading to over-intervention and unintended semantic drift. In addition, many methods rely on manually crafted counterfactual supervision, such as surrogate prompts, which incurs substantial data construction costs that limit scalability to new concepts. To address these limitations, we propose GRACE, a structured concept erasure framework designed to enable localized and selective intervention. Specifically, we introduce a semantically weighted sensitive subspace estimation to precisely lock intervention directions, and employ lightweight subspace-constrained adapters to prevent global semantic disturbance. To eliminate the dependency on manual prompt engineering, we design an automatically decoupled safe-anchor mechanism. To mitigate semantic drift induced by excessive intervention, we introduce an energy-driven dynamic gating mechanism that adaptively controls the timing and strength of intervention at inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves a superior balance between erasure effectiveness and generation fidelity. Compared with the average performance of five state-of-the-art (SOTA) concept erasure methods, our method improves the fine-grained NSFW reduction rate by $17.86\%$, while reducing the macro-averaged target CLIP Score and preservation-oriented Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) by $4.55\%$ and $52.14\%$, indicating stronger concept suppression with substantially improved preservation of the original model's generative utility.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Counting Events, Not Seeing Them: Diagnosing and Repairing the Readout Failure in Video LLMs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video LLMs fail conspicuously at counting how many times an object crosses the screen, a failure attributed to missing object permanence. Using construction-grounded synthetic testbeds with validated labels, we show this attribution is incomplete: the count signal is present but unread - linear probes decode per-window presence at 93% while global count decoding collapses to a duration confound. Concurrent work reports the same representation-output dissociation for repetition counting; we show that in exit-and-reappear event counting it is repairable: two readout-directed repairs (episode-localization supervision and a discrete event-symbol side channel) raise same-object counting from 46.7% to 65.0% (oracle 66.7%) on a chance-33% benchmark across 7B-30B systems. Transfer to an independent factory costs nothing, and a measurement audit exposes five data-integrity failures that had obscured the boundary. A real-video audit (REALCOUNT, n=18, blind-audited) shows the boundary persists - best 55.6% at chance 33.3% - and symbol transfer fails zero-shot. A 1-epoch in-domain adaptation bench is negative (six levers at 28-50%), but 3 epochs reverse this for the symbol channel: with oracle timelines the reader reaches 94.4% sequence-disjoint (and 100% strict on the full set), while the deployed 2-epoch head reaches 61.1% in all three seeds (42-44), no better than a shuffled-symbol control (61.1% seed 42, 66.7% seed 43), and one clip above the unadapted reader (55.6%). The residual gap is detector evidence, not reader capacity: the same reader reaches 72.2-88.9% on GT timelines. The failure is repairable with informative timelines, but the deployed head remains the bottleneck; a frozen-feature boundary probe is weak (AUC 0.62 vs. 0.51 permutation) and non-transferring (0.77 within-clip vs. 0.62 across windows).
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures, 8 tables. Preprint v2 (2026-11-10). Corrected-prompt retrain; Tables 5-8 updated; Appendix A item 5 closed. Comments welcome

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Split and Bridge: Multimodal Generation via Diffusion Bridging
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Visual data are often expressed through multiple complementary modalities (e.g., images and segmentation masks), each capturing different aspects of the same underlying structure. Most existing multimodal methods adopt a top-down paradigm, learning a shared latent variable through joint training from scratch, which limits scalability. We propose Split and Bridge (SnB), a bottom-up framework for multimodal generation that couples pretrained unimodal diffusion models at sampling time. Rather than learning a unified latent space, SnB generates coherent multimodal samples by following a shared diffusion trajectory up to a split point and then branching into modality-specific trajectories guided by a bridge module. This design enables plug-and-play reuse of powerful pretrained models without joint training, making it scalable and easily adaptable. Across standard benchmarks (PolyMNIST, CelebAMask-HQ) and more complex settings (PIE-Bench++, ROCO), SnB achieves a strong balance between sample quality and coherence. We show that SnB naturally extends to downstream zero-shot tasks such as interleaved co-generation, image editing, and style coupling/decoupling. Our results demonstrate that bottom-up generation provides a practical framework that complements existing top-down multimodal approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/AhmadArrabi/SnB

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for multimodal and embodied tasks, yet aggregate accuracy or consistency alone does not reveal whether a judge changes its verdict for the right reason. We propose State-Conditional Invariance (SCI), a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome. We instantiate SCI in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with aligned Full, evidence-removal, and counterfactual variants, plus presentation and representation probes. Across five diagnostic tasks, GridWM-Judge tests local perception, action-conditioned transitions, presentation stability, representation exchangeability, and Full-CF causal discrimination. Our diagnostic evaluations reveal heterogeneous failure modes, including sensitivity to evidence presentation and encoding, low activation on successful trajectories, and weak paired counterfactual discrimination. Perception-controlled analyses further indicate that visual grounding and objective recovery are substantial, model-dependent bottlenecks. These results motivate jointly reporting correctness, presentation stability, and causal sensitivity instead of relying on a single score.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 (Track on Evaluations and Datasets). 47 pages, 16 figures. Project page: https://xinyuw922-pixel.github.io/Towards-Reliable-VLM-Judge/ ; Code: https://github.com/xinyuw922-pixel/Towards-Reliable-VLM-Judge ; Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/nahco318/Towards-Reliable-VLM-Judges

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: With Tools or Because of Tools? Tracing Capability Gains in Multimodal Agents
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Tool-augmented multimodal agents show strong benchmark gains, often taken as evidence that agents have learned to use tools. We argue that this interpretation can be premature: a tool-call trace alone does not show whether the tool supplied answer-critical information. We study two representative ``thinking with images'' agents, Thyme and DeepEyesV2, across real-world understanding, OCR, chart understanding, and mathematical reasoning. Each agent is compared with its Tool-Free counterpart and with a Pure-Text Reasoner trained from the same source pool without tool-calling trajectories. Tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement, does not reliably reduce generated-token cost, and leaves only a small tool-only solved set: 93% of DeepEyesV2's tool-solved problems and 96% of Thyme's are also solved by at least one non-tool setting. Mechanism ablations further show that the full tool-use loop does not consistently outperform either the tool-call format or the returned execution result alone. In the settings we study, the analyzed agents appear to learn tool-calling patterns more reliably than tool-contributed capabilities, suggesting that evaluation should distinguish tool availability from whether tools actually expand what agents can solve.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Astrocyte-Centric 3D Reconstruction across Normal and Stress-associated Ultrastructural States
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The morphology of astrocytes is closely associated with their ability to support and modulate neural circuit functions; however, its reconstruction from volume electron microscopy (vEM) data remains labor-intensive and computationally resource-intensive, placing substantial barriers on its broader adoption and scalability despite the high spatial resolution of vEM. We present AstroSeg-vEM, a lightweight, astrocyte-centric framework for morphology-preserving astrocyte segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and quantitative morphological analysis in vEM images. AstroSeg-vEM combines transformer-based 2D segmentation with dedicated post-processing methods and operates directly on high-resolution EM sections, making it well suited to anisotropic vEM data and downstream proofreading workflows while preserving the full in-plane resolution of the original EM data. Across four mouse hippocampal datasets representing normal and morphologically defined stress-associated astrocyte ultrastructural states, AstroSeg-vEM demonstrates robust performance and generalization, achieving average Dice and weighted Dice values of 0.92 and 0.95, respectively, on a held-out test dataset. Its lightweight architecture enables efficient, high-fidelity reconstruction on consumer-grade hardware, providing a scalable and accessible platform for large-scale astrocyte ultrastructure analysis and future astrocyte-neuron interaction studies.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted for publication in npj Imaging. 19 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables, including Supplementary Material. Code is available at https://github.com/QuIN-Lab/AstroSeg-vEM

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. For each caption, PhyRubric constructs a caption-specific rubric before any video is seen, decomposing the caption into semantic and physical items, and derives scores from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped evidence. We instantiate this framework as PhyRubric-Bench, which spans 34 categories across five physical domains, and scale it up to PhyRubric-Train with 3,788 videos, on which we fine-tune the open-source PhyRubric-Judge. Empirical results across ten T2V models show that physical commonsense remains far from solved, and that PhyRubric-Judge correlates more closely with human judgments than existing open-source judges while matching the frontier proprietary Gemini 4 Argon. Further analysis provides actionable insights for T2V models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Mixture of Cognitive Experts in Large Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) require strong reasoning over both visual and textual inputs. Recent work suggests that cognitive elements, especially diverse representations and metacognition, correlate with better performance. Many required perceptual functions are already provided by specialized domain-specific computer vision models, which can serve as the perceptual subsystem for detecting objects, localizing them, inferring states, recovering spatial layout, and reading text. The key challenge is integrating these multi-encoder experts into a trustworthy, interpretable, and coherent representation that improves verifiability and reduces hallucinations. This is difficult because vision-language questions span different cognitive levels, yet most LVLM pipelines apply the same perception-reasoning routing regardless of the query's demands. We propose an evidence-driven multimodal reasoning framework that uses a Bloom-inspired taxonomy as a hierarchical reasoning protocol. Our two-stage cognitive verbalization first produces a Literal Evidence Summary by decomposing expert outputs into short, atomic evidence statements, then performs Bloom Verbalization to convert these items into a staged reasoning trace. A lightweight Reasoning Trace Module quantitatively analyzes the trace, making evidence usage and reasoning progression explicit. Experiments show improvements in both perception and reasoning and diagnostics indicate that different queries induce different cognitive entry levels and evidence-use trajectories.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CoMet: Context and Multiplicity Decomposition for Multimodal Uncertainty Estimation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Uncertainty estimation has been a long-standing challenge in AI models; it amounts to "knowing what you don't know," and metacognition is notoriously difficult even for humans (cf. the Dunning-Kruger effect). Although it is still far from solved even in simpler classification systems, tackling it in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is becoming increasingly important. Within MLLMs, uncertainty can stem from any of the diverse sources as well as from their relationships, and further can stem from the unbounded answers in the open-ended setting. To tackle the issues, we propose CoMet, an MLLM uncertainty estimation method by decomposing uncertainty into a context-specific term and a multiplicity-specific term. The former captures ambiguity induced by the given context (e.g., task or prompt), while the latter captures how many plausible answers determined by the context remain compatible with the given input. We train a lightweight post-hoc uncertainty module to estimate these quantities, which enables efficient uncertainty estimation without autoregressive answer generation or repeated sampling. Experiments on various open-ended multimodal benchmarks, hallucination detection, and multiple-choice visual question answering benchmarks show that CoMet consistently improves uncertainty estimation over existing baselines while remaining efficient in practice. Code is available at https://github.com/princetonvisualai/comet_uncertainty

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Spatially-Aware Class-Agnostic Object Counting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Generalised object counting aims to estimate the number of instances of an arbitrary object category from a single image, but many recent methods can struggle on structurally complex objects due to limited spatial modelling. We present \textit{UpCount}, a class-agnostic counter designed to better preserve spatial structure. UpCount strengthens the visual representation by extracting multi-layer features from a ViT-B/16 encoder and reassembling them into a refined multi-scale pyramid that is spatially refined using Dense Prediction Transformers and FeatUp, yielding features with improved structural and spatial sensitivity; a proposal--verification counting head then identifies repeated patterns and produces a density map for the final count. On FSC-147, UpCount achieves 12.39 MAE and 100.89 RMSE on the test set, and it transfers effectively to vehicle counting on CARPK (6.27 MAE, 8.79 RMSE). Code: https://github.com/r28112072-rgb/upcount

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Are Text-to-Image Models Inductivist Turkeys? A Counterfactual Benchmark for Causal Reasoning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) generation models have achieved remarkable progress in producing visually realistic images from natural language prompts. Yet it remains unclear whether their success reflects genuine causal understanding or sophisticated pattern matching over visual-textual correlations. Inspired by Russell's inductivist turkey, we introduce Counterfactual-World (CF-World), a counterfactual benchmark designed to investigate whether text-to-image models can generate images under rules that systematically contradict real-world priors. CF-World organizes each scenario into three progressive levels: factual generation under ordinary world knowledge, explicit counterfactual generation with direct visual instructions, and implicit counterfactual generation requiring causal deduction from altered rules. We evaluate open-source and closed-source text-to-image models using CF-Eval, a scoring pipeline based on vision-language models. We report the scores at each prompt level as the primary results and use Prior Resistance Rate (PRR) and Reasoning Retention Rate (RRR) as auxiliary descriptive indicators. All evaluated models score lower on counterfactual prompts than on factual prompts. Diagnostic experiments reveal difficulties in following altered rules and recombining rarely co-occurring visual attributes. The gains from rephrasing object and attribute names are consistent with a role for learned visual priors in counterfactual generation. Our benchmark and evaluation code are publicly available at https://jylei16.github.io/CF-World.github.io/.

Graphics.title: A Lightweight Differentiable Method for Real-Time Skin Rendering and Digitization
Graphics.summary: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines. We bridge this gap by directly estimating subsurface scattering parameters tailored for real-time rendering pipelines. We introduce a differentiable Screen-Space Subsurface Scattering (SSSS) framework that enables the joint optimization of spatially varying base textures and scattering distances. To account for local variations in skin thickness, we estimate these parameters across distinct facial regions, generating a blended profile map ready for production runtime engines. Our pipeline utilizes a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture setup designed for accessible and practical appearance acquisition. Optimization is driven by a masked loss function targeting regions where subsurface scattering effects are dominant. We validate our approach on a real-world dataset of $45$ individuals across the Monk Skin Tone Scale, ensuring demographic generalization. Furthermore, we complement this evaluation with synthetic data, a multi-light setup validating our single-light assumption, and a tilted-view configuration confirming angular consistency. Results demonstrate that our method effectively recovers scattering parameters from lightweight inputs, yielding realistic skin appearance directly compatible with standard real-time shaders.
Graphics.comment: 20 pages, 25 figures; includes 6 pages of supplementary material. Accepted to Computers and Graphics

Graphics.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
Graphics.summary: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

Graphics.title: Exploring Cross-Reality Transitions between Projections and Head-Mounted Displays for Immersive Digital Art
Graphics.summary: Immersive exhibitions increasingly combine large-scale projections with mixed reality (MR) head-mounted displays (HMDs), but how users perceive transitions across these heterogeneous visualization environments remains underexplored. We investigate cross-reality (CR) object- and scene-level transitions in a hybrid immersive art installation spanning projection, augmented reality (AR), and virtual reality (VR). In a within-subjects study (N=24), we compared a calibrated condition with a bundled inconsistency condition introducing noticeable differences in spatial alignment, visual appearance, and cross-device latency. This contrast was used not to establish perceptual thresholds or hardware targets, but as a diagnostic probe to make transition disruptions more perceptible and discussable. The inconsistency condition reduced presence and increased workload. Interviews showed that spatial misalignment disrupted action-outcome predictability, appearance mismatch reduced aesthetic coherence, and latency weakened perceived responsiveness. Effects also varied by asset type: rigid static assets exposed inconsistencies more clearly, animated skeletal assets shifted attention toward motion, and particle effects often masked small discrepancies. These findings clarify how users perceive projection-MR transitions and support asset-aware design strategies for coherent hybrid immersive art. We also release HUICRSync, an open-source Unreal Engine plugin for prototyping projection-MR CR experiences.

Graphics.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
Graphics.summary: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.

Graphics.title: Physics-Driven Extraction of Dynamic Fluid Asset from Monocular Video with Generative 3DGS
Graphics.summary: Existing methods for dynamic 3D scene synthesis from video rely on per-frame deformation fields optimized through pixel-level reconstruction losses. While effective for closed systems such as elastic solids, these approaches face challenges with open systems like fluids where material continuously enters and exits the scene, topology changes freely, and no stable point correspondence exists across frames. We propose a simulation-driven alternative that optimizes the parameters of a fluid simulator to reproduce dynamics observed in a single-view video, rather than fitting per-point deformation to pixel values. Our framework leverages generative 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models to obtain initial fluid geometry including unseen surfaces, estimates a physically grounded velocity field from surface motions with a physics-constraint correction algorithm, and converts it into a divergence-free, grid-based representation. A differentiable Affine Particle-In-Cell (APIC) simulation then optimizes effective simulation parameters, such as viscosity, boundary conditions, and inflow/outflow velocities, to match the observed dynamics. Because the dynamics are governed by forward simulation, the output assets are inherently editable, interactive, and temporally extendable, which reconstruction-based approaches cannot readily provide. Stage-wise ablations confirm that each stage is necessary, and hyperparameter sweeps show the pipeline to be robust without sensitive per-scene tuning. Our method handles various liquid fluids, including inviscid and viscous types, demonstrating the potential for automatically creating simulation-ready 3D fluid assets from readily available internet videos.
Graphics.comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics. 21 pages (18 pages + 3 pages supplementary material), 28 figures

Graphics.title: Pygmalion Effect in Vision: Image-to-Clay Translation for Reflective Geometry Reconstruction
Graphics.summary: Understanding reflection remains a long-standing challenge in 3D reconstruction due to the entanglement of appearance and geometry under view-dependent reflections. In this work, we present the Pygmalion Effect in Vision, a novel framework that metaphorically "sculpts" reflective objects into clay-like forms through image-to-clay translation. We then introduce a dual-branch design in which a BRDF-based reflective branch and a clay-guided branch share the same Gaussian geometry but operate through independent rendering paths. The clay-guided branch, supervised by the synthesized clay images, provides reflection-free geometric guidance that complements the photometric supervision of the BRDF branch. Experiments on both synthetic and real datasets show consistent improvements in both geometry and photometric metrics. Beyond technical gains, our framework reveals that seeing by unshining, translating radiance into neutrality, can serve as a powerful inductive bias for reflective object geometry learning.

Graphics.title: Deformable Texture Maps: Compiling Dynamic Microgeometry into Neural Textures
Graphics.summary: Deformable material surfaces, such as cloth, owe their appearance to fine-scale geometries that restructure under deformation. Even when coarse simulation models efficiently recover this microstructure, explicitly instantiating and rendering it remains expensive. We introduce Deformable Texture Maps (DTM), a representation that compiles deformation-driven microgeometry into a continuous and compact neural texture. Our model maps texture coordinates and local deformations to intrinsic maps describing opacity, surface normals, depth, and material identity. This captures the occlusion and visibility changes generated by deformation. At runtime, these maps provide a common texture-space representation of deformation-driven fine-scale structure that can be evaluated directly on coarse deforming surfaces. Since our representation encodes geometric attributes rather than radiance, lighting and material response remain decoupled from the learned model. This allows us to apply relighting, as well as shading and material editing without retraining. We further introduce a persistent texture-space rendering strategy that caches these intrinsic maps and selectively updates them as deformation changes. This effectively decouples neural evaluation from frame rendering and enables their reuse across frames and conventional rendering effects. We demonstrate our approach on yarn-based textiles, where non-linear material stretch and shear induce changes in yarn geometry, spacing and occlusion. We build our model by, first, sweeping tileable yarn patches through deformation space, then, rendering the detailed geometry into a canonical texture-space, and finally, compressing the resulting maps into a single neural representation. Our resulting model can be evaluated directly on arbitrary coarse garment meshes and integrated with conventional shading pipelines, keeping appearance authorable at render time.

Graphics.title: Patch-Based Generalized Neural Texture Upscaling
Graphics.summary: We propose a lightweight neural texture upscaling method. A single generalized MLP is trained on a diverse collection of texture patches and integrated into the texture sampling stage, upscaling low-resolution textures on-the-fly at rendering time. Because the model is generalized rather than overfit to specific content, no per-asset training is required - the same model applies to any existing scene without modifying texture data or the asset pipeline. Storing lower-resolution base textures reduces disk footprint, upscaling at sampling time eliminates the need to store high-resolution textures in VRAM, and sharing a single set of model weights across all textures ensures non-divergent GPU execution. We evaluate our method across multiple texture classes, demonstrating consistent improvement over analytic upscaling methods in perceptual quality.

Multimedia.title: LUMIR: Decoupled Multimodal Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Data for Next-POI Recommendation
Multimedia.summary: As multimodal tourism-related information collected from heterogeneous data sources has become increasingly available, learning effective representations has attracted attention for improving recommendation performance. Existing approaches often tightly couple multimodal fusion with the architecture and optimization objective of a specific downstream model, which limits the generality and reusability of the learned representations. To address these limitations, we propose LUMIR, a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework based on contrastive learning. Multimodal information collected from heterogeneous data sources is first semantically unified into a shared textual representation space using large language models (LLMs). An interaction-aware fusion mechanism is then designed to model cross-modal interactions, while sequential signals are incorporated as a structural constraint to guide representation learning. To evaluate the learned representations, experiments are conducted on a multimodal point-of-interest (POI) dataset under the next-POI recommendation setting across multiple sequential recommendation backbones. The results show that LUMIR consistently outperforms existing multimodal fusion baselines in both accuracy-oriented and beyond-accuracy metrics, demonstrating that decoupling representation learning from downstream optimization provides an effective paradigm for learning reusable multimodal representations. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/wzehui/LUMIR.
Multimedia.comment: 16 pages. Accepted at the DaQuaMRec Workshop, co-located with ACM RecSys 2026

Multimedia.title: Data Quality Challenges in Multimodal Tourism Recommender Systems
Multimedia.summary: Modern recommender systems increasingly consider diverse data modalities to enhance model performance. However, the quality of the underlying multimodal data (e.g. data from social media platforms) has received limited attention so far. Focusing on tourism recommendation, we examine real-world challenges encountered when using datasets from Yelp and Instagram. Issues include noise from fake reviews, hallucinated content from LLMs, modality contradictions, and demographic bias. We outline future directions such as quality-aware fusion, structured and controlled LLM-based content generation to reduce hallucinations, and user group differentiation to improve the robustness and reliability of multimodal recommendation systems.
Multimedia.comment: 4 pages. Presented at the DaQuaMRec Workshop, co-located with ACM RecSys 2025

Multimedia.title: Joint Activation and Weight Quantization for Learned Image Compression
Multimedia.summary: Learned image compression (LIC) models achieve competitive rate-distortion performance with increasingly large networks, making network quantization important for efficient deployment. Directly quantizing LIC models remains difficult in post-training quantization (PTQ) because compression performance is highly sensitive to quantization noise. Existing methods typically focus on optimizing either the weights or the activations, resulting in substantial rate-distortion degradation. To address this limitation, we introduce a two-stage pipeline that uses SmoothQuant to balance activation and weight ranges, followed by GPTQ to adapt the transformed weights. The proposed joint search framework optimizes the balancing transformation and adapted weights under the rate-distortion objective, accounting for the coupling between the two stages. Experiments across multiple LIC architectures and activation quantization configurations show that the joint search strategy consistently reduces rate-distortion degradation after quantization.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted at IEEE VCIP 2026. 5 pages, 3 figures

Multimedia.title: Unified Synthesis of Compositional Speech and Sound from Free-Form Text Prompts
Multimedia.summary: Generating unified audio that naturally integrates speech and sounds from free-form text prompts remains challenging. For example, the prompt ``A fast drum roll ends with a cymbal crash, after which a man shouts: `Come on!'.'' describes several events that should appear in order and form a coherent recording rather than independent tracks that lack coherent temporal and semantic interactions. Current methods broadly follow two paradigms: pipeline methods couple separate text-to-sound and text-to-speech models, while unified models rely on a single generator that still requires structured, multi-field prompt inputs. Both paradigms require upstream prompt decomposition or rewriting, limiting free-form flexibility and risking cascading errors. To enable direct generation from free-form prompts within a single model, we introduce PlanAudio, an end-to-end framework that maps unconstrained free-form text to unified audio without intermediate prompt preprocessing. To address the challenges of direct free-form generation, PlanAudio integrates latent planning into a single autoregressive framework, predicting continuous audio layout before acoustic token synthesis. We construct a large-scale training corpus and introduce Free-Form Unified Audio Generation Benchmark (FUAG) for evaluation, both spanning speech, sound, and joint speech-and-sound generation. Experiments show that a single PlanAudio outperforms existing pipeline and unified baselines on speech-and-sound generation, while remaining competitive with specialist models on speech and sound generation. Further analysis validates the effectiveness of audio layout planning over textual planning, acoustic planning, and direct generation. Sample Available: https://planaudio.github.io/PlanAudio2026/.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026. This version renames concepts, reorganizes sections, and fixes Method notation; adds ablation experiments and core-mechanism analysis; updates Table 1 with larger training data (improved speech performance in speech-and-sound mixed scenarios). The main conclusions remain unchanged

Multimedia.title: DASWeave: Weaving Evidence across Speaking Conditions for Multimodal Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Screening
Multimedia.summary: Multimodal screening for depression, anxiety, and stress in children and adolescents uses verbal and nonverbal behaviour. Most existing multimodal methods learn from a single recording or interview. Yet a participant's behaviour changes with the speaking condition, and these changes hold evidence that is invisible in a single recording. We propose DASWeave to bring this evidence into a neural network that encodes each response and then combines all responses of a participant. We train supervised trees to find which behavioural statistics matter for screening, both within each response and in how they change across conditions. We feed the tree outputs into the network both before and after this combination. We fine-tune a large language model to relate what a participant says to how they say it across conditions, and feed its representation into the network after the combination. The language model reads behaviour as text descriptions. We therefore derive additional training targets for the network from a multimodal large language model that takes in the audio-visual features directly. On the official hidden test set of the ACM Multimedia 2026 AdoDAS Grand Challenge (Track 1), DASWeave ranks second among 95 eligible teams. Its mean F1 is 27.1% higher than that of the official audio-visual baseline. It also has the highest mean AUROC among the top five teams. Ablation studies on the validation set show that the supervised trees and the fine-tuned language model contribute most to mean F1.

Multimedia.title: Smiling Regulates Emotion During Traumatic Recollection
Multimedia.summary: We study when, where, and why 978 Holocaust survivors smile in video testimonies. We create an automatic smile detection model from facial features with an F1 of 85% and annotate detected smiles under two established taxonomies of smiling. We produce narrative features on 1,083,417 transcript sentences as well as emotional valence from three different modalities: audio, eye gaze, and text transcript. Smiling rates are associated with specific semantic topics, narrative structures, and temporal syntaxes across the corpus. Smiles often occur during periods of intense negative affect and we find negative-affect smiles are associated with more positive subsequent valence trajectories across all three modalities. Smiling reduces eye dynamics and blink rates, with both of these effects modulated by narrative valence. Taken together, we conclude that smiling plays a critical role in regulating emotion and social interaction during traumatic recollection.
Multimedia.comment: Received Best Paper Runner-Up Award at ICMI 2026

Graphics.title: A Unified Interactive Framework for Real-Time Three-Dimensional Cellular Automata Simulation in XR
Graphics.summary: Integrating three-dimensional cellular automata (3D CA) into extended reality (XR) requires coordinated simulation, volumetric data management, rendering, and interaction under variable hardware constraints. This paper presents a hybrid study combining a critical review of existing approaches with a unified architecture for real-time 3D CA in XR. The proposed five-layer architecture integrates voxel and rule management, parallel computation, interoperability middleware, visualization, and XR interaction. Its key principles include hardware-aware execution, asynchronous simulation-rendering, adaptive fidelity, and cross-engine interoperability. An analytical evaluation framework is defined to assess performance, latency, scalability, memory efficiency, simulation correctness, and interaction quality. The proposed framework provides a foundation for developing portable and interactive 3D CA systems across desktop and mobile XR platforms.

Graphics.title: DinoComplete: 3D Shape Completion with Distilled Semantic Priors and State Space Models
Graphics.summary: 3D shape completion from partial scans remains challenging for unseen categories and noisy real-world observations, where geometry alone is often insufficient for inferring missing structure. We present DinoComplete, a deterministic and efficient shape completion framework that augments geometric reconstruction with voxel-aligned semantic priors distilled from DINO features. First, we construct multi-view DINO feature volumes aligned with ShapeNet data and train a student network to predict dense semantic features directly from incomplete shapes. These predicted features capture global structure and part-aware semantic context while remaining aligned with the underlying geometry. We then integrate these distilled features into a completion network, where geometric and semantic voxel representations are fused through voxel state-space modeling. To enable efficient long-range reasoning without sacrificing resolution, we introduce a Multi-Scale Voxel Mamba module that refines the fused features by combining full-grid and chunk-wise sequence modeling. Experiments on unseen ShapeNet categories and ScanNet objects show that DinoComplete achieves competitive completion quality than prior deterministic and generative based completion methods while using relatively fewer parameters, requiring lower memory, and achieving faster inference. Our results demonstrate that distilling semantic priors from visual foundation models improves generalization and robustness in 3D shape completion.

Graphics.title: Spaghetti Splatting: Differentiating Curvilinear Dirac Masses via Convolution
Graphics.summary: In production systems, 3D geometry is represented by primitives such as points, lines, and triangles, as rendering hardware is optimized to generate images from them very efficiently. Learning such primitives from images by volume rendering is challenging, as they are Dirac masses defined at infinitesimal locations in space. EWA splatting, Poisson reconstruction, and 3D Gaussian Splatting overcome this by convolving Dirac masses with a low-frequency kernel, a recipe that generalizes along two axes: the kernel and the primitive. As points and triangles have already received significant attention, we investigate this recipe for curvilinear primitives, and introduce Spaghetti Splatting. We approximate curves by polylines whose convolution converges to that of the continuous curve, and volume render each segment so that connected segments composite without overcounting at their joints. For fast training and inference, we linearize the camera projection per segment, which also accommodates kernels beyond Gaussians, such as Beta kernels. As a point is a curve of zero length, our representation is a strict superset of 3D Gaussian Splatting. It remains competitive with the state-of-the-art on general scenes, outperforms methods specialized to line-like geometry, natively supports anti-aliasing, and produces long connected strands that are directly amenable to physics simulation.

Graphics.title: PL Morse-Cerf Theory for Topological Analysis of Time-Varying Scalar Fields
Graphics.summary: Morse-Cerf theory studies the evolution of critical points in one-parameter families of smooth functions defined on a manifold. This paper describes an adaptation of Morse-Cerf theory of smooth functions to one-parameter families of piecewise-linear (PL) functions. The vertex diagram and Cerf diagram are introduced as topological descriptors that represent evolution of the PL function. The characterization of a crossing in the vertex diagram based on the homology of the lower links of vertices leads to the definition of a topological descriptor for time-varying scalar fields. Algorithms and methods for computing, querying, and comparing Cerf diagrams support its application towards the analysis of time-varying scalar fields. Stability theorems on the comparison measure provide a guarantee of robustness. Experimental results on multiple scientific datasets demonstrate its practical utility.
Graphics.comment: Extended journal version of the previous IEEE VIS 2025 Short Paper, PrePrints https://doi.org/10.1109/VIS60296.2025.00024

Graphics.title: Explicit LOD-Conditioned Anisotropic Filtering for Neural Texture Compression
Graphics.summary: Neural texture compression (NTC) stores material textures compactly, but the dominant feature-pyramid design receives no filtering from the GPU texture unit: it learns each material at a fixed UV and level of detail and has no explicit anisotropic-filtering (AF) mechanism. Setting the filter from the footprint aspect ratio alone is not enough: a single input cannot carry both the shape of the footprint and its size, so the image is too blurry near the camera by the same amount at every distance. Our method, AF-NTC, instead conditions the decoder on the same three bounded values a hardware sampler uses: minor-axis scale (LOD), aspect ratio, and major-axis orientation. These drive a tap line along the major axis and a level blend across the minor axis, and we train against anisotropically filtered ground truth. At $25\%$ of a full BC7 mip chain, AF-NTC beats the no-AF trilinear-BC7 baseline on all ten material--scene pairs we compare ($+1.3$ to $+7.6$\,dB), and it is $0.0$ to $3.4$\,dB below the $4\times$-larger anisotropic-BC7, depending on the material.

Graphics.title: Dynamic Elliptical Graph Factor Models via Riemannian Optimization with Geodesic Temporal Regularization
Graphics.summary: Inferring time-varying graphs from high-dimensional nodal observations is challenging when windows contain fewer samples than nodes, observations are heavy-tailed, and the dependence drifts multiplicatively over time. We propose the dynamic elliptical graph factor model (\textsc{Degfm}), combining: an elliptical likelihood that down-weights outliers; a low-rank-plus-diagonal (LRaD) parameterization of each precision matrix, shown to be the posterior precision of a field conditioned on a few aggregate linear measurements; and a temporal regularizer given by the squared affine-invariant distance between consecutive precision matrices, capturing multiplicative evolution and invariant to node rescaling and to the choice between precision and covariance. Estimation on a product of quotient manifolds is solved by a safeguarded Riemannian conjugate-gradient method with closed-form temporal gradients via generalized eigendecompositions. We prove that (i) LRaD is locally identifiable modulo orthogonal transformations under a tangent-space transversality (coherence) condition; (ii) with rank-preserving Armijo backtracking, the solver is well defined and converges to critical points with $\min_{k<K}\|\grad F(θ^{(k)})\|^2=\mathcal{O}(1/K)$; (iii) a localized estimator obeys a finite-sample oracle inequality whose error scales with the intrinsic dimension $pr+p-r(r-1)/2$ times an effective temporal dimension decreasing from $1$ to $1/T$ as coupling strengthens, quantifying the variance reduction and bias of temporal coupling, and extending to misspecified non-LRaD models; (iv) for Student-$t$ observations, the local restricted strong convexity is proved rather than assumed, with curvature of order $ν/(p+ν)$ shown unimprovable; and (v) partial-correlation graphs are recovered exactly by thresholding. Experiments on synthetic data, S\&P~500 returns, and HCP fMRI data validate the approach.

Graphics.title: X-SiT: Inherently Interpretable Surface Vision Transformers for Dementia Diagnosis
Graphics.summary: Interpretable models are crucial for supporting clinical decision-making, driving advances in their development and application for medical images. However, the nature of 3D volumetric data makes it inherently challenging to visualize and interpret intricate and complex structures like the cerebral cortex. Cortical surface renderings, on the other hand, provide a more accessible and understandable 3D representation of brain anatomy, facilitating visualization and interactive exploration. Motivated by this advantage and the widespread use of surface data for studying neurological disorders, we present the eXplainable Surface Vision Transformer (X-SiT). This is the first inherently interpretable neural network that offers human-understandable predictions based on interpretable cortical features. As part of X-SiT, we introduce a prototypical surface patch decoder for classifying surface patch embeddings, incorporating case-based reasoning with spatially corresponding cortical prototypes. The results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in detecting Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia while additionally providing informative prototypes that align with known disease patterns and reveal classification errors.

Graphics.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
Graphics.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic, real-time rendering on commodity GPUs and is increasingly adopted in generative world models and autonomous driving simulators. However, existing optimizations rely on algorithmic changes that often require retraining, or on specialized accelerators that lack flexibility across evolving 3DGS variants. In this paper, we identify a fundamental inefficiency in GPU-based 3DGS rendering: severe SM-level load imbalance caused by uneven workloads across screen tiles. This imbalance creates a long execution tail, leaving most SMs idle while a few process computationally intensive tiles, particularly in large-scale urban scenes. To address this, we present a software-defined GPU scheduling approach that mitigates the execution tail. Our approach uses a persistent kernel to schedule heavy tiles first and selectively chunks outlier tiles across multiple CTAs. A lightweight per-frame policy determines when and how much to chunk using tile statistics already available in the rendering pipeline. Our approach requires neither retraining nor specialized hardware and can be applied orthogonally to existing optimizations across diverse 3DGS variants. Averaged per scene, it accelerates alpha blending by up to 2.93x on a large-scale urban scene, and by up to 5.6x on its most imbalanced frames, while retaining the original alpha blending formulation.

Graphics.title: Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation
Graphics.summary: Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.

Graphics.title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path
Graphics.summary: We present a real-time method for reconstructing fully integrated pixel radiance in rendered volumetric media under direct and ambient environmental illumination, using compact, low-cost scene features and statistics. Unlike Monte Carlo denoising pipelines for volumetric rendering, which depend on computationally expensive path-traced radiance estimates, our approach directly infers the final light-transport solution from inexpensive primary-ray and environment sample evaluations. We show that these features form a near-sufficient representation of the scene, enabling accurate reconstruction at substantially lower computational cost. Using an attention-augmented image-to-image network, we demonstrate that complete pixel radiance can be inferred directly from these auxiliary features, without requiring the original radiance signal. Operating in image space also provides a more stable computational cost as the camera zooms into or out of the volume, with substantially less dependence on volume density than approaches based on explicit multiple-scattering simulation. We demonstrate real-time performance and high reconstruction accuracy in challenging volumetric cloud scenarios.

Graphics.title: Architectural Textured Proxy Generation
Graphics.summary: Textured proxy models are a fundamental representation for architectural scenes, enabling efficient rendering while preserving visual fidelity. Existing approaches construct such proxies through a sequential pipeline in which geometry is first abstracted from a dense reconstruction and textures are later projected from input images. This geometry-only formulation neglects image evidence during proxy generation, leading to misalignment of structural features such as facades, edges, and their intersections across views. As a result, inconsistencies are deferred to a downstream correction stage during texturing, where the underlying geometric structure can no longer be reliably recovered. In this work, we introduce an image-guided proxy formulation in which proxy generation is jointly constrained by both the dense reconstruction and the input aerial images. By incorporating image derived structural cues directly into the construction process, the proxy is optimized to align with observed features across views from the outset, rather than relying on post hoc correction that may be infeasible. This shift from a geometry-only to an image-guided paradigm produces proxies that are inherently consistent with the input imagery, enabling more accurate geometry and more coherent texture mapping. We realize this formulation through a framework that extracts structural priors from images and dense geometry, and enforces their consistency during proxy optimization. The resulting proxies exhibit improved alignment of structural features, reducing artifacts such as edge duplication, texture drift, and cross view inconsistencies. Experiments on diverse architectural scenes demonstrate that our approach produces compact, geometry texture aligned proxies with substantially improved visual fidelity compared to existing methods.

Multimedia.title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking
Multimedia.summary: Temporal Sentence Grounding (TSG) aims to localize temporal segments in untrimmed videos that correspond to natural language queries, a critical task for video understanding with applications in video retrieval, summarization, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant progress driven by transformer-based models, existing TSG methods suffer from two key limitations: quantization errors due to temporal downsampling, which misalign segment boundaries, and suboptimal ranking of predictions based on semantic matching rather than localization precision. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Boundary Refinement and Ranking (ABRR) framework, a novel, model-agnostic post-processing approach that enhances the performance of any TSG model without retraining. ABRR integrates three innovative components: (1) Temporal Distribution Smoothing, which mitigates noise in predicted score distributions using Gaussian kernel convolution; (2) Boundary Refinement via Optimal Transport, which leverages the 2-Wasserstein distance and Sinkhorn iterations to align coarse segment boundaries with true temporal moments, grounded in Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport theory; and (3) Quality-Driven Re-Ranking, which reorders predictions using a composite score balancing localization precision and semantic relevance. By correcting quantization errors and prioritizing accurately localized segments, ABRR achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art TSG models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions, and QVHighlights, demonstrate consistent gains at stringent IoU thresholds (e.g., IoU=0.7), alongside enhanced ranking performance. The framework's computational efficiency and compatibility with existing models make it a versatile and impactful solution for real-world TSG applications.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Multimedia

Multimedia.title: Multimodal Judges Flag, Humans Decide: A Review-and-Edit Framework for AI-Generated Product Video Ads
Multimedia.summary: Generative pipelines can now turn every product page of an e-commerce catalog into a short video ad, but deciding whether such an ad is usable is not one good-or-bad call.
