Every edit is a list of slider values a person can read and adjust. The same model can drive any editor that makes those changes; we test RawTherapee and darktable. We train on 10M photographs from a commercial stock collection and test on FiveK, PPR10K and SPAQ. Nine quality judges score every edit, and in a user study 157 human raters made 9,253 choices between our edit and another method's edit of the same photograph. When Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Astra edit the same photographs in the same editor, raters prefer our edits to GPT-6 Astra's (54.3%) and rate them even with Claude's (50.5%). We also compare with supervised retouchers on their home ground: NeurOP on FiveK and AdaInt on PPR10K, each trained on that set's own expert edits. Raters chose our edits in 46.3% of those comparisons. ATune, a 54M-parameter model trained without a single expert edit, now matches frontier models at setting an editor's sliders.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 27 pages, 12 figures, 18 tables. Main paper 8 pages plus supplementary material

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Disentangled Embedding Optimization for Diffusion-Based Dataset Distillation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Dataset distillation aims to compress large-scale datasets into compact synthetic subsets that enable efficient model training with comparable performance to the original data. Recent advances show that diffusion models are highly effective for this task due to their strong generative capability. Existing diffusion-based approaches typically perform class-wise clustering and use the obtained cluster prototypes as diffusion inputs to generate distilled samples. However, the uniformly distributed original samples in a category inevitably lead to entanglement near cluster boundaries, pulling the cluster prototypes closer and reducing the inter-cluster separation. Consequently, the diffusion model receives overly similar latent inputs, resulting in synthetic data with limited diversity. To address this issue, we propose Disentangled Embedding Optimization (DEO), a simple yet effective framework that replaces static clustering with trainable embeddings. These embeddings are optimized to match the Gaussian statistics (i.e., mean and covariance) of the original data distribution, while a diversity regularizer is designed to encourage separation among these embeddings to improve the intra-class variability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed DEO can generate more diversified and representative distilled data than existing cluster-based diffusion methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance and superior generalization across multiple datasets.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures. Accepted at the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM 2026)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of $432$ strictly paired test cases across $48$ executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a $3 \times 3$ factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. Extensive evaluations across $12$ representative models reveal that: (I) world preservation and visual realization remain in stark operational tension; (II) richer draft scaffolding anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and (III) conflicting source cues trigger severe source leakage (up to $64\%$), exposing fragile cross-modal disentanglement. To mitigate these bottlenecks, we propose WorldDraft-Primer, a plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that consistently improves both objectives across frozen video renderers. Together, WorldDraft and WorldDraft-Primer lay a foundation for bridging programmatic 4D simulation with video generation, advancing physically grounded generative rendering.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SPEM: Scan-Prior Entropy Modeling for LiDAR Point Cloud Compression
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: LiDAR point clouds exhibit scan-induced spatial regularities that are informative for geometry compression. Existing scan-aware approaches often exploit these regularities by transforming coded geometry into spherical or beam-aligned coordinate systems. However, this couples acquisition priors with geometry representation, altering spatial partitioning and quantization, and potentially preventing exact recovery of the original Cartesian geometry. We argue that acquisition priors should guide probability modeling rather than dictate the coding representation. We propose SPEM, a Scan-Prior Entropy Modeling framework that exploits LiDAR scanning regularities within the entropy model without requiring coordinate transformation. We introduce a multi-frequency spherical rotary positional encoding that captures scan-aligned spatial relationships in both backbone self-attention and decoded-context retrieval. Building upon this encoding, we develop a decoded-memory autoregressive predictor that efficiently exploits previously decoded occupancy information through reusable key/value caches. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both lossy and lossless LiDAR geometry compression, highlighting the effectiveness of scan-prior modeling across different coordinate representations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: When can multi-fragment 2D/3D registration be trusted? Calibrated certification and uncertainty-driven view planning for pelvic fracture fluoroscopy
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Registering a segmented CT to fluoroscopy can locate every fracture fragment but can guide surgery only when trusted. After each shot, our closed loop registers all fragments, bounds their errors with a calibrated sandwich covariance, flags implausible or ambiguous ones, and stops or plans the next view. On simulated fluoroscopy of 60 held-out fracture CTs with realistic image uncertainty, 95% bounds covered 83% of unflagged fragments and 91% of those within 5mm, but from the second view on 14% failed by over 5mm, a third with bounds of at most 2mm. A fragment's shift when a view was added separated tightly bounded failures best (exploratory; AUC 0.94, bound 0.81). Requiring that the newest view moved no fragment beyond its bound, preferred post hoc, lowered false stops at 2mm from 23% to 6% overall, with 345 instead of 362 correct ones but more trajectories uncertified; delaying the stop did not, and other signals at equal acceptance left 10-15% false. With a segmentation error shared by all views (median Dice 0.89), 21% of this rule's stops were false against 10% without it (15 cases; exploratory). Minimax planning certified sooner than the clinical protocol without the check (4.20 versus 4.72 shots, Holm p <0.001), but no criterion reached the pre-specified endpoint, a true 2mm error, significantly sooner, even in the true basin. On real fluoroscopy of five intact pelves no 2mm certificate was false. Trust takes evidence across views, not only a calibrated local bound.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SurgStreamer: proactive, request-driven monitoring of surgical video streams with structured state and a reusable reasoning layer
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Surgical teams could benefit from assistants that watch the video for requested events, such as "tell me when the clip applier appears during Calot triangle dissection", and answer questions about what has already happened. We formalise this task as request-driven event detection with exact semantics and causal alert decisions, and present SurgStreamer. It separates procedure-specific perception, which maps the 1-FPS stream to a structured state over tools, actions and phases, from procedure-agnostic reasoning, which evaluates a formal monitoring condition over this state and an event memory, either with exact rules or with a small controller that addresses entities through pointers rather than names. We evaluate this monitoring core with gold conditions. On a pre-registered, sealed test set of 12 laparoscopic cholecystectomies, SurgStreamer reached a macro event-F1 of 0.598 over full procedures. On identical 75-s windows with only the window available to every method, it scored 0.677. The tested configurations of the streaming vision-language model OneStreamer-4B, including ones fine-tuned on SurgStreamer's state or on video with an adapted vision encoder, scored at most 0.540 (Holm-adjusted p <= 0.012). At three external centres, re-training only perception raised performance on held-out procedures from 0.239 to 0.470. On a new procedure, pituitary surgery, controller weights trained on cholecystectomy matched an in-domain controller on oracle state (0.947 vs 0.938). On predicted state they missed the pre-registered non-inferiority margin (-0.024 [-0.040, -0.008]) unless the alert thresholds were re-calibrated. The results support separating perception from reasoning and point to perception under distribution shift as the main limitation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GOOSELoc: A Multimodal Benchmark for Ground-to-Aerial Localization in Unstructured Off-Road Terrain
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Cross-view pose estimation estimates a ground camera's geographic pose by matching onboard sensor data with geo-referenced overhead imagery. This is particularly relevant when GNSS is unreliable, for example under forest canopy or in urban canyons. Existing metric cross-view benchmarks, such as VIGOR and cross-view KITTI, are dominated by urban and road scenes with strong human-made structure without off-road terrain. We introduce GOOSELoc, a multimodal benchmark for ground-to-aerial localization in unstructured environments, including forests, fields, and rural tracks. GOOSELoc comprises 9,356 scenes recorded across all four seasons around Munich, Germany, pairing geo-referenced aerial orthophotos with surround-view RGB imagery and 3D LiDAR point clouds. Paved/unpaved labels enable analyzing the impact of terrain structure, while the seasonal recordings allow studying the appearance gap to mostly summer-captured orthophotos. To assess the transferability of existing methods, we adapt and fine-tune four state-of-the-art cross-view localization baselines on GOOSELoc. Despite task-specific fine-tuning, the performance degrades substantially in off-road environments. We therefore propose a multimodal baseline combining surround-view imagery and LiDAR geometry, improving localization performance and providing a stronger reference for future work. Data and baselines are released at https://gooseloc.github.io.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Expanding the Role of Diffusion Models for Robust Classifier Training
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Incorporating diffusion-generated synthetic data into adversarial training (AT) has been shown to substantially improve the training of robust image classifiers. In this work, we extend the role of diffusion models beyond merely generating synthetic data, examining whether their internal representations, which encode meaningful features of the data, can provide additional benefits for robust classifier training. Through systematic experiments, we show that diffusion models offer representations that are both diverse and partially robust, and that explicitly incorporating diffusion representations as an auxiliary learning signal during AT consistently improves robustness across settings. Furthermore, our representation analysis indicates that incorporating diffusion models into AT encourages more disentangled features, while diffusion representations and diffusion-generated synthetic data play complementary roles in shaping representations. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet validate these findings, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly leveraging diffusion representations and synthetic data within AT.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Split-and-scale Latent 3D Representations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models. Despite this progress, current representations struggle to capture the fine details of complex objects, fundamentally limited by the capacity of their latents. However, scaling latent capacity at training time is computationally expensive and often infeasible under memory limits, and naively increasing the number of latents at inference fails to make effective use of the added capacity. In this paper, we address both challenges with \textit{split-and-scale}, a method that effectively expands latent capacity at inference while keeping training cost tractable. Our key observation is that by representing 3D scenes as continuous functions of 3D coordinates, a single pretrained tokenizer can be applied at inference to arbitrarily small sub-regions of a scene, allocating the same latent capacity to a smaller spatial extent and thus capturing far higher detail. We validate this insight by conducting extensive ablations to study the trade-offs between compute, memory, latent capacity, and reconstruction quality, demonstrating our inference-time scaling method achieves quality competitive with much larger models that exceed single-GPU memory limits. We further demonstrate that split-and-scale supports high-quality generative modeling, training an autoregressive 3D generator that performs competitively with state-of-the-art baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Museum records express how people understand heritage objects through cultural and historical relations. Recovering these human attributions from images is a technical challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for image-only recovery of title, culture, period, origin, and creator. Its evaluation framework distinguishes field-level from complete-record compatibility and uses human validation for semantic judgement. Across nine VLMs, mean field accuracy is 36.16--49.82%; 7.20--17.02% of records have all four contextual fields compatible, and 2.13--7.87% have all five, including title. For the two tested models, image-only input yields 12.6--32.2 percentage points higher reference compatibility for culture, period, and origin than a museum-and-title-only control.

Graphics.title: BrickFlow: Connectivity-Guided Brick Reconstruction
Graphics.summary: Given a set of LEGO parts and an image of an assembled object, our task is to infer the pose of each part to assemble the object. In contrast with traditional 3D reconstruction, doing so requires satisfying discrete physical constraints, which provide structure but render the problem combinatorial and highly sensitive to small pose errors. To learn a prior over how parts fit together, we train a set-conditioned SE(3) flow model on procedurally generated assemblies. We then finetune this model to inject image conditioning, using 1% as much data. However, while the learned flow captures global structure, it does not enforce connectivity. To address this, we introduce an analytic connectivity-field guidance to pull predictions toward connected assemblies at test time. Through this, we demonstrate improved build quality with model size, pretraining, and guidance. We make our models and data available for research purposes at https://kulits.github.io/BrickFlow/

Graphics.title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
Graphics.summary: Interactive video-to-video applications require real-time generation while maintaining long-range temporal consistency. However, recent methods achieve speed by restricting attention to a fixed-length causal window. This limits long-range consistency whenever relevant history falls outside the context window. To address this limitation, we introduce vid2vid-long, a correspondence-based approach grounded in a simple observation. Video-to-video translation provides an explicit cross-frame reference: the regions that match in the input video should match in the output video too. Concretely, we compute patch-level correspondences in the input, guiding retrieval of previously generated outputs in the corresponding regions, and condition the model on these patches through correspondence cross-attention. Our experiments demonstrate that vid2vid-long consistently improves long-range temporal consistency across recent video models while preserving generation quality and real-time performance.

Graphics.title: Neural Render Proxies for Interactive and Differentiable Lighting
Graphics.summary: Within the CG animation production pipeline, the challenges artists tackle in Lighting can be immense. Even minor adjustments require re-rendering massive scenes with slow offline renderers; global illumination has to be sampled and complex shaders have to be evaluated, leading to iteration times of minutes to hours per frame. To accelerate this process, we introduce a novel neural render proxy (NRP) that enables differentiable relighting of static scenes with fixed camera and materials at interactive rates. Our main insight is the decoupling of traditional rendering into path sampling and emission computation. From a single, light-agnostic render pass, we collect light transport data in the form of path samples. This enables rapidly sampling lighting conditions on the fly, and training a scene-specific lightweight neural network that learns how light is transported from any scene location to any image pixel. This approach is compatible with non-differentiable production renderers, induces minimal memory requirements during inference, and scales only with resolution and the number of light sources and parameters, but independently of scene and appearance complexity. Our evaluation demonstrates interactive frame rates for relighting (~30-60 Hz) while closely approximating the visual fidelity of ground-truth path tracing. In addition, the differentiable NRP enables fast, gradient-based inverse workflows, allowing artists to efficiently solve for lighting parameters from intuitive image-space edits or generative targets.
Graphics.comment: Accepted at Computer Graphics Forum (Proc. EGSR 2026)

Graphics.title: Sprint3D: Accelerating End-to-End 3D Asset Generation through Pipeline Optimization
Graphics.summary: Image-to-3D generative models now produce asset-quality textured meshes, but at minutes per asset they remain slow to iterate with and costly to deploy. Prior work has mostly accelerated the sampling of the networks, and where it also optimizes the mesh processing, it trains its own generators. We instead start from a publicly released pipeline and ask how much of its end-to-end time can be saved. Profiling the public Pixal3D pipeline shows that its latency is dominated by what happens after the networks: the four rectified flows take 14% of the wall-clock time and mesh post-processing takes 85%, most of it in CPU-based UV unwrapping. We therefore first rebuild the mesh post-processing on the GPU and take it off the critical path, then cut the per-evaluation overhead of the flows and distill them from 76 to 8 network evaluations. The resulting pipeline, Sprint3D, reduces the median time per asset from 133 s to 4.05 s on one H200 GPU at the same export settings (33$\times$). At the same time, on 2,653 held-out Toys4K objects it improves every input-view normal metric of the Pixal3D protocol, with a slightly lower mean silhouette IoU, lower point-cloud alignment scores and less fine texture detail. The rebuilt post-processing alone also speeds up TRELLIS.2, which uses the same export code, by 6.7$\times$ without a detectable change in the evaluated metrics.

Graphics.title: PIM: A Physical Intuition Model for Low-Latency Prediction of Object Interaction Outcomes
Graphics.summary: Predicting object interaction outcomes from initial conditions is a central problem in data-driven physical reasoning. Existing methods often use rigid-body-level states or predict the evolution through autoregressive rollouts. Coarse representations cannot represent local deformation, while rollout errors may compound over long prediction horizons. Instead, we introduce PIM, a Physical Intuition Model that directly predicts a physical system's equilibrium state from its initial mesh geometry, kinematics, and physical attributes. PIM combines local k-nearest-neighbor (KNN) attention to encode intra-object geometry, anchor-based cross-object attention to model interactions, and a dual-branch decoder that predicts object-level translations and per-vertex residual displacements. Across MuJoCo scenarios involving both rigid and deformable interactions, PIM achieves lower vertex and centroid errors than the evaluated baselines. By predicting complete equilibrium states in a single forward pass, PIM substantially reduces latency relative to autoregressive learned models and MuJoCo rollouts under the evaluated protocols, enabling low-latency inference when only the final outcome is required.

Multimedia.title: Augmented Hybrid TV Services. Habits, Preferences, Opinions and Expectations of Spanish Consumers
Multimedia.summary: The convergence of hybrid broadcast and broadband delivery, companion devices, and immersive technologies enables new forms of interactive, personalized, and accessible TV services. This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Hybrid TV services and presents an exploratory user requirements and preliminary acceptance assessment for 5 representative use cases. They were selected through an exploratory stakeholder consultation and 3 co-design workshops with audiovisual professionals and participants from organizations supporting people with visual or hearing impairments. They combine conventional TV with complementary content delivered to connected devices, including AR/VR HMD. They were subsequently evaluated through a cross-sectional CAWI survey of 626 Internet and connected TV users in Spain. Each participant viewed standardized video demonstrations of 2 randomly assigned cases and assessed their perceived usefulness, anticipated benefits/limitations, and interest in them. The results show substantial interest across all five use cases, ranging from 64.7% to 76.9%. Adaptive and personalized augmented subtitles received the highest level of interest and were particularly valued for their accessibility, language-learning, and personalization benefits. Immersive services involving complementary AR content, virtual screens, 3D objects, and 360 video were also evaluated positively, although participants identified device cost, ergonomics, connectivity, usability, and synchronization as anticipated limitations. The findings provide user-centered evidence that can inform the prioritization, design, and subsequent prototype-based evaluation of standards-compliant Augmented Hybrid TV services. Because the study assessed video-based scenarios rather than functional systems, the results represent perceived usefulness and stated interest rather than observed adoption or technically validated QoE.
Multimedia.comment: 26 pages, 12 figures and 16 tables

Multimedia.title: RADIANT: Redundancy-Aware Information Allocation for Universal Multi-Modal Fusion
Multimedia.summary: Universal multi-modal fusion often fails not because modalities are insufficiently aligned, but because the fusion process allocates information poorly: redundant evidence is repeatedly amplified, modality-unique evidence is over-smoothed during alignment, and task-dependent synergistic evidence is insufficiently activated. We present RADIANT (Redundancy-Aware Dynamic Information Allocation Network), a task-general framework that organizes fusion around three complementary roles: suppressing redundant cross-modal overlap, preserving modality-unique evidence, and composing task-conditioned synergy through cross-modal interaction. Specifically, stable matrix-exponential projections are used to reduce interference among shared and modality-unique streams, while task memory with hard positive updates selects which synergistic interactions should be activated for the current fusion regime. Extensive experiments across six heterogeneous fusion tasks show consistent improvements over the compared methods. On FLIR, RADIANT improves downstream detection mAP@0.5 from 91.2% to 96.8%, a gain of 5.6 percentage points (6.1% relative) over GIF. RADIANT also exhibits strong direct cross-dataset transfer, with further gains from inference-time task-memory adaptation while keeping all network weights frozen. Additional ablations and sensitivity studies support the robustness of the allocation mechanism.
Multimedia.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures. Published in ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26). Code: https://github.com/StevenWSH27/RADIANT

Multimedia.title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
Multimedia.summary: Museum records express how people understand heritage objects through cultural and historical relations. Recovering these human attributions from images is a technical challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for image-only recovery of title, culture, period, origin, and creator. Its evaluation framework distinguishes field-level from complete-record compatibility and uses human validation for semantic judgement. Across nine VLMs, mean field accuracy is 36.16--49.82%; 7.20--17.02% of records have all four contextual fields compatible, and 2.13--7.87% have all five, including title. For the two tested models, image-only input yields 12.6--32.2 percentage points higher reference compatibility for culture, period, and origin than a museum-and-title-only control.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SFL-Net: Dependence-Regularized Latent Pathways for Multi-Contrast MRI-to-tau-PET Synthesis and Component Attribution
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Structural MRI-to-tau-PET synthesis estimates molecular imaging patterns from indirect anatomical correlates. We present SFL-Net, a vector-quantized architecture with shared, T1-specific, FLAIR-specific, and joint-input latent pathways. Dependence regularization differentiates these pathways, while latent-derived structural conditioning supports decoding without direct encoder-decoder feature skips. We evaluated SFL-Net and capacity-matched VAE, VQ-VAE, U-Net, and SPADE-U-Net variants using 605 training and 83 internal validation subjects pooled from ADNI-3 and OASIS-3. SFL-Net achieved the lowest raw PET MAE and MSE and the highest PSNR among the implemented models, while SPADE-U-Net variants performed better on several SUVR and staging metrics. Exact coalitional Shapley attribution assigned the largest average marginal contribution to the joint-input pathway, with substantial variation across subjects. These contributions describe decoder dependence under latent replacement and retained structural conditioning; they do not establish identifiable information-theoretic synergy or the incremental benefit of combining MRI contrasts. Predictions showed dynamic-range compression at higher tau burden, and several staging metrics were close to a constant Stage 1 reference. SFL-Net provides a framework for structured latent-component interrogation in multi-input image synthesis, linking architectural pathways to reconstruction behavior.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Design, Implementation and Evaluation of a Real-Time Remote Photoplethysmography (rPPG) Acquisition System for Non-Invasive Vital Sign Monitoring
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The growing integration of smart environments and low-power computing devices, coupled with mass-market sensor technologies, is driving advancements in remote and non-contact-based physiological monitoring. However, deploying these systems in real-time on resource-constrained platforms introduces significant challenges related to scalability, interoperability, and performance. This paper presents a computationally efficient real-time remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) system, designed to extract physiological signals, such as heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation (SpO2), from facial video streams. The system is built on the Face2PPG pipeline, which processes video frames sequentially for rPPG signal extraction and analysis, while leveraging a multithreaded architecture to manage video capture, real-time processing, network communication, and graphical user interface updates concurrently. This design targets continuous operation at 30 frames per second (FPS), with adaptive feedback through a collaborative user interface to guide optimal signal capture conditions. The network interface includes both an HTTP server for continuous video streaming and a RESTful API for on-demand vital sign retrieval. To ensure accurate performance despite limited computational resources, we use a hybrid programming model combining Functional Reactive Programming (FRP) and the Actor Model, allowing event-driven processing and efficient task parallelization. We evaluate HR accuracy on three public datasets (COHFACE, LGI-PPGI, and UBFC-RPPG), and conduct preliminary evaluations of RR on COHFACE and SpO2 on PURE. We also assess the processing time and end-to-end operation of the system on two computers, including live HR and SpO2 agreement with a medical-grade fingertip pulse oximeter across five 10-minute sessions. Our work addresses key challenges in real-time contactless biosignal monitoring.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 33 pages, 4 figures, 11 numbered equations, 6 tables, and 67 references. Evaluated on 4 public datasets and in 5 live 10-minute sessions on 2 computers. Code available at https://github.com/Multimodal-Sensing-Lab/rt-rppg

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Steering Away from Memorization: Reachability-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-Image Diffusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image diffusion models are susceptible to memorization, revealing a fundamental failure to generalize beyond the training set. Current mitigation approaches often sacrifice image quality or prompt alignment to reduce memorization. To address this, we propose Reachability-Aware Diffusion Steering (RADS), an offline-trained, sampling-time control framework that mitigates memorization while maintaining generation fidelity. RADS models the diffusion denoising process as a dynamical system and learns a policy-conditioned reachability value function that estimates future memorization risk along the denoising trajectory. This motivates a constrained reinforcement learning (RL) formulation, where a policy learns to steer the trajectory away from memorization via perturbations in the caption embedding space. Empirical evaluations show that RADS achieves a stronger empirical Pareto frontier between generation diversity (SSCD), quality (FID), and alignment (CLIP) compared to state-of-the-art inference-time baselines. Crucially, RADS applies the learned controller during sampling time, separating memorization mitigation from the pretrained model. Our website is available at: https://s-karnik.github.io/rads-memorization-project-page/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ReflFlow: Learning Geometry-Guided Ray Tracing for Dynamic Specular Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present ReflFlow, a novel framework for high-fidelity rendering of dynamic specular scenes by addressing two key challenges: precise reflection direction estimation and physically accurate modeling. To achieve this, we propose a Residual Material-Augmented 2D Gaussian Splatting representation that models dynamic geometry and material properties, allowing accurate reflection ray computation. Furthermore, we introduce a Dynamic Environment Gaussian and a hybrid rendering pipeline that decomposes rendering into diffuse and specular components, enabling physically informed specular synthesis via rasterization and ray tracing. Finally, we devise a coarse-to-fine training strategy to improve optimization stability and promote physically meaningful decomposition. Extensive experiments on dynamic scene benchmarks demonstrate that ReflFlow outperforms prior methods quantitatively and qualitatively, producing sharper and more realistic specular reflections in complex dynamic environments.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: ICML 2026. 16 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables, including references and appendices

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DUNE: Disentangling Polysemantic Neurons Without Losing Predictive Performance
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely used, but understanding what they actually learn remains difficult. A major obstacle is that individual neurons often respond to multiple unrelated concepts, obscuring the network's internal decision process. Existing approaches, such as sparse autoencoders, can disentangle these mixed signals into more meaningful, ``monosemantic'' features, but typically introduce approximation errors that may degrade downstream performance. Consequently, these methods exhibit a Pareto frontier between monosemanticity and functional faithfulness. To address this, we introduce DUNE (disentangling units with no error), a method that decomposes DNN neurons into more monosemantic subunits while preserving their original function by design. DUNE identifies concept-specific contributions from the preceding layer and re-routes them into separate subunits whose aggregation exactly recovers the original activation. DUNE can be applied directly to pretrained models, without labels or training of an auxiliary model. Across several models, including DINOv2, DUNE achieves state-of-the-art or competitive monosemanticity while exactly preserving functional faithfulness, substantially advancing the existing Pareto frontier between these properties. DUNE operates efficiently and enables fine-grained interventions such as concept-specific steering.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Does Seeing More Mean Knowing More? Mono-Anchored Advantage Normalization for Multi-Source Visual Reasoning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Visual reasoning through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has achieved remarkable progress. However, when dealing with multi-source inputs, existing approaches tend to treat them as a mere accumulation of information, lacking explicit mechanisms to distinguish whether integrating additional sources yields information gain or introduces interference. Therefore, they struggle to effectively model dynamic interaction when integrating multiple sources, particularly when they differ significantly in physical properties and semantics, e.g., infrared and depth, leading to inferior performance to mono-source reasoning when a certain source holds the dominant signal. To address this issue, we propose MARS, a novel mono-anchored multi-source reasoning framework that models each visual modality as an independent information source. Specifically, by treating mono-source rewards as dynamic anchors, our method explicitly incorporates the information gain introduced by multi-source fusion into advantage normalization and adaptively emphasizes mutual promotion between sources while suppressing potential noise or conflicts during RLVR. From theoretical analysis, our method effectively quantifies information gain introduced by multi-source integration in gradient estimation, enabling consistent modality regulation. Empirical results also show impressive 3.2% and 4.9% performance gains on GRPO and DAPO across diverse datasets, confirming the effectiveness of our method. Code is available at https://github.com/AI9Stars/MARS.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Diffusion Plug-in Priors for Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Ultrasound videos suffer from hardware-constrained spatial resolution and signal-dependent speckle, while paired low- and high-resolution acquisitions are rarely available. We propose UltraDiff, a self-supervised framework for joint ultrasound video super-resolution and despeckling that uses a frozen pre-trained diffusion model as a plug-in prior. Rather than retraining the model, UltraDiff restores each frame by optimizing the sampler's latent seed under a range-constrained maximum a posteriori-inspired formulation. We derive a speckle-aware data-fidelity term from a Rayleigh scale-family model and characterize its relative-residual and locally variance-adaptive weighting properties. To address degeneracy near zero intensities, we introduce a stabilized surrogate fidelity that is bounded below and strictly convex in log intensity for positive observations in its unclamped form. Total-variation regularization complements the removal of mixed noise, and a temporal seed update warm-starts each frame from the optimized seed of its predecessor, accelerating the convergence. On EchoNet-LVH with simulated speckle and additive noise, UltraDiff with a natural-image prior improves peak signal-to-noise ratio by 1.24\,dB over the strongest baseline, and ultrasound-related priors yield further gains. On 100 real EchoNet-Dynamic videos, UltraDiff reduces the mean absolute error of zero-shot ejection fraction prediction from 7.31 to 6.37 percentage points compared with DUP. These results support ground-truth-free ultrasound video restoration using frozen diffusion priors and a speckle-aware fidelity, without paired training data or model retraining.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Pothole Risk Assessment with Geometrically Grounded Vision Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Potholes impose billions of dollars in annual vehicle damage, yet detectors report only where potholes are, not how severe they are or what to do. Judging severity from a single RGB image is ill-posed, and ungrounded vision-language model (VLM) assessments tend to be over-conservative. We present a five-stage modular framework for the offline assessment of already-detected potholes that combines geometric measurements with VLM reasoning: perspective transformation, zero-shot SAM segmentation, geometric feature extraction, Gemini 2.5 Pro severity classification with composite risk scoring, and natural-language warning generation. We evaluate it on 3,092 potholes in 1,119 dashcam scenes against independent references. Severity agreement with a prediction-free three-annotator panel is weak (Cohen's $κ= 0.139$, 95% CI [0.00, 0.28]; $n = 101$) and far below the annotators' agreement with one another ($κ= 0.605$); against physically measured depth on an independent RGB-D dataset, it is also weak ($κ= 0.098$), although the predicted classes preserve the order of measured depths. The severity classes are therefore perceived visual categories, not depth measurements. Geometric grounding does change the warnings: relative to an image-only baseline, it moves 26.7% of scenes out of the high-urgency tier and raises critical-tier assignments by 109% (Stuart-Maxwell $p < 10^{-15}$), and in a blind study, three raters preferred the grounded warnings 3.5:1. A six-arm prompt ablation attributes the hybrid prompt's rule adherence to the per-pothole measurements rather than to the rubric or worked examples. At USD 0.105 per scene, it suits large-scale offline infrastructure assessment; its maneuver suggestions are advisory research outputs, not validated vehicle guidance.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 17 tables. Submitted to IEEE Access. Code and data: https://github.com/malekaburaddaha/Pothole_Assessment_Pipeline

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Sub-actions in Action: Text-Guided Hand-Role Alignment for Sub-Action Recognition
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Our objective is to enhance VLMs ability to distinguish the roles of the left and right hands in egocentric actions. We introduce sub-action detection, a task that requires models to explicitly recognise the left- and right-hand roles and their manipulated objects within an ongoing high-level action. To address this challenge, we propose BiScopeNet, a framework that augments existing video-LLMs without modifying their vision encoders or language models. BiScopeNet incorporates two components: FocusAlign, a gated text-guided attention-based module that selectively aligns video features with textual context to emphasise action-relevant cues, and MetaLoss, a masked, object-weighted loss that prioritises visually grounded terms. To supervise sub-action detection, we introduce BiScopeCap-100K, a large-scale video-level dataset curated from existing egocentric datasets, providing dense captions that jointly describe high-level actions, left/right-hand roles, and manipulated objects, enriched with spatial metadata for grounding. Across the evaluated Video-LLM backbones, BiScopeNet improves action, hand-role, and object recognition over the corresponding supervised baselines, achieving the strongest aggregate performance among the evaluated configurations on BiScopeCap.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at BMVC 2026, Supplementary material is available

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AVI-HT: Adaptive Vision-IMU Fusion for 3D Gloved Hand Tracking
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present AVI-HT, an adaptive visual-IMU fusion approach for tracking 3D hand poses by jointly modeling the egocentric images with on-glove 6-DoF IMU signals. AVI-HT significantly improved accuracy and availability, particularly in hand-object interaction (HOI) scenarios involving heavy visual occlusion. Two complementary ingredients underpin its success: (1) synchronized multi-modal training data pairing on-body vision-IMU sensor streams with ground-truth 3D hand poses from a motion-capture system, and (2) a cross-sensor deep attention mechanism that adaptively modulates the trust assigned to the vision and individual IMU sensors. To evaluate AVI-HT in real-world settings, we conduct extensive experiments on our DexGloveHOI dataset that consists of 100K+ pairwise vision-IMU samples with synchronized 3D annotated poses, in which users manipulate a variety of objects during daily tasks. We compare against multiple single- and multi-modal tracking approaches under two hand models (UmeTrack, MANO). The results show that AVI-HT reduces mean keypoint error by 16.1% and its wrist-aligned variant by 24.2% over the baselines. A hand-object contact evaluation shows that AVI-HT keeps finger contacts with the manipulated object more accurately and consistently over time, reducing contact losses by 8.5%. Ablation studies further show that our fusion design outperforms simpler schemes and that the gains grow with occlusion and hold across subjects.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an imperceptible budget of 1/255, SuperVLAD and BoQ keep at most 0.2% top-1 recall (R@1) on four benchmarks. We propose anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT), which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive and an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model. Checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance, and the full trade-off is reported. Within five validation R@1 points of clean cost, plain adversarial training has no admissible checkpoint, whereas ARAFT raises robust R@1 from zero to 47.3 on SuperVLAD and 55.3 on BoQ; plain adversarial training exceeds this only at about three times the clean cost. Against unbudgeted plain adversarial training on the test sets, ARAFT matches its robust R@1 at 2/255 with about ten more clean R@1 points. At 4/255, plain adversarial training is 6-9 robust R@1 points ahead, while ARAFT still keeps its ten-point clean advantage. Developed on SuperVLAD, ARAFT transfers to BoQ without re-tuning, and its robustness holds against stronger optimisers, with no sign of gradient masking.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Topology-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Videos
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reconstructing dynamic scenes and objects from monocular egocentric video is crucial for embodied AI, yet existing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approaches struggle with everyday interactions involving topological changes, such as cutting, assembly, opening, or closing. Since 4DGS methods rely on deforming a fixed representation, events that split, merge, or reveal surfaces cause severe visual artifacts. To address this challenge, we introduce TopoEgo, the first benchmark dedicated to topological changes in egocentric video (covering fission, fusion, open, and close), alongside Topo-4DGS, a topology-aware reconstruction method. Topo4DGS jointly models part-level motion and time-varying surface support by assigning independent rigid transformations to interacting parts and dynamically activating or deactivating Gaussians as surfaces appear, disappear, or separate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Topo-4DGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 4DGS approaches across topological changes, especially on post-event frames. Code and data will be made publicly available.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Language moved from many task-specific models to one unified model: a single generative model with a single generative training task that handles all of them within the same backbone, and keeps improving with data, parameters and compute. We believe the bitter lesson applies just as much to computer vision, 3D and spatial understanding, in the end to visual intelligence: the effort should go into general architectures that solve all these tasks in a unified way, and into scaling them, rather than into task-specific designs. We test this on monocular geometry, a task that has belonged to specialised architectures for years. Iris-Z is a general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together. A single backbone denoises, reasons about and understands the image and its depth at the same time, and one set of weights generates images with their depth, estimates depth from photographs and paints images onto a given depth. At enough scale it surpasses state-of-the-art specialists on established depth benchmarks while keeping the generative abilities of the backbone it started from without specialized layers. We release two models for the community.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables. Code and models: https://github.com/speridlabs/iris-z-sdk

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Predicting the Needle in a Petabyte Scale Haystack: Open-Vocabulary Event Anticipation in Satellite Imagery
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Satellite constellations now image the Earth daily, capturing the lifecycle of events from deforestation to urban construction. Anticipating these events before completion enables timely intervention, yet existing systems cannot jointly identify where a change occurs, what it will become, and when it will finish across an open vocabulary. Building such a model requires diverse event data, but events are like needles in a haystack, making manual annotation at global scale infeasible. We address this problem by representing change as the vector difference between vision-language model embeddings at distinct time points. This arithmetic approach allows us to search for semantic transformations directly in the latent space, enabling (1) an automated data engine for global event discovery without manual annotation and (2) the largest global satellite event dataset to our knowledge, comprising 21,000+ locations across 64+ event types with ~2M images from PlanetScope and Sentinel-2 spanning six continents, to train (3) a novel global-scale event anticipation model. Our model detects change with a 93.5% max F1 score, outperforms baselines 3.6x on predicted event retrieval, and forecasts completion dates with a 3-day median error, even nine months before completion. Code: https://github.com/ShreelekhaR/predicting-the-needle
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 29 pages, 9 figures, to be published in NeurIPS 2026

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Adaptive Distance Detection and Adaptive Instance Segmentation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: This paper is about object detection model and semantic segmentation model in an FPS game Counter Strike: Condition Zero to detect enemies. Semantic segmentation is pixel-wise detection algorithm. We customized the architecture for semantic segmentation. We used YOLOv5s to train object detection model. After training, the inference time of semantic segmentation was compared to object detection. It was observed that object detection was slightly faster and semantic segmentation is slower but better at detecting the exact shape of the object. However, we found out that this slight difference of inference can grow exponentially if the both models get more complex. To solve this, we propose a novel approach called Adaptive distance detection which combines both algorithms. We will also introduce Adaptive instance segmentation to combine semantic segmentation and panoptic segmentation.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: This is the paper from my Bachelor's degree in University of Birmingham

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GraftRay: Physically Based Mesh Insertion into Gaussian Splatting Scenes via Path Tracing
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present GraftRay, a unified method for physically consistent insertion of mesh objects into 2D and 3D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS/3DGS) indoor scenes. We lift albedo, roughness, metallic and normals from diffusion-based 2D priors onto the Gaussians by back-projection, model windows and lamps as analytic area emitters, and recover their absolute radiance from ordinary LDR captures with a low-dimensional fit over unit-radiance bases. A path tracer over Gaussians and meshes then produces view-consistent shading, interreflections and soft shadows, which are composited onto the original reconstruction by differential rendering, preserving the untouched background. On synthetic, real and generated scenes, GraftRay outperforms recent insertion and inverse-rendering baselines in image fidelity and shadow accuracy at competitive cost, and users prefer its lighting and shadows over those of the baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TRACE: Trajectory Synchronization for Training-Free Resolution Extension in Video Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: More text-to-video models are available, but many remain limited to low resolutions. Training them for higher resolutions is costly, while existing training-free methods still struggle with fine detail, scene structure, and efficiency. We propose TRACE, a training-free method that synchronizes low- and high-resolution generation trajectories. During early denoising, TRACE aligns predicted scene content at corresponding noise levels. It computes high-resolution updates from low-resolution predictions and the current high-resolution state, without high-resolution model inference. The high-resolution trajectory retains fine-grained variation for generating new details. Local window attention then refines fine details in a shared high-resolution latent state. TRACE checks suspected duplicate subjects against the corresponding low-resolution layout and corrects selected regions and their solver history while preserving detail elsewhere. Experiments across all kinds of video generation backbones and resolutions show improved perceptual quality and text-video alignment over FreeSwim, a state-of-the-art training-free method, with 2.0-2.9x end-to-end speedups. Our code and models will be released at https://github.com/libozhu03/TRACE.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Learning from paired modalities is commonly equated with aligning them: two encoders are trained until the embeddings of a pair coincide in a shared space. We study whether cross-modal retrieval and classification can instead be obtained while the two encoders' own embedding spaces remain directly unaligned. DuoJEPA trains one encoder per modality with the self-supervised LeJEPA objective and appends to each encoder a single transformer layer that translates its embedding into the other encoder's space, supervised by a contrastive objective computed entirely within that target space. No loss term compares the two own spaces directly, although the encoders are optimised jointly through the translation objective. In our experiments, the translator's residual connections determine where the cross-modal pressure is absorbed: with a residual translator the two encoders become directly aligned, whereas with a skipless (residual-free) translator a paired-cosine test detects no alignment in the final models, and at most a weak one in the ablations, at comparable cross-modal performance. The learned class-token translation is well approximated by a single scaled rotation of the source space. We evaluate DuoJEPA on two modality pairs that differ in nearly every respect. On chest radiographs and reports from CheXpert Plus, it attains a zero-shot AUC of 86.6 and a cross-modal retrieval score of 78.5, compared with 60.0 and 64.2 for our reimplementation of LeVLJEPA with the same encoders and data. On Sentinel-2 optical and Sentinel-1 radar imagery, the frozen encoders fall within the range of published Sentinel foundation models under our reproduction of the Copernicus-Bench linear-probe protocol, the translator retrieves the paired image of the other sensor among 4,000 candidates in 77-79% of cases, and a patch-level extension transfers the within-image similarity structure of the scene.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Addressable Memory for Video World Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We study visual persistence in interactive video world models. These models rely on a Key-Value (KV) cache as a growing visual memory to carry forward previously generated frames. However, we find that models can no longer reliably address stored content once rollouts extend beyond the training horizon, because temporal Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) offsets can exceed the training range and the model struggles to retrieve the relevant visual information through attention. Moreover, naively compressing the cache in the RoPE-rotated space degrades memory by averaging keys with incompatible positional phases. To address this, we propose WorldTrace, a training-free memory framework for long-horizon visual persistence. WorldTrace keeps compressed memory addressable by assigning each summary slot a distinct, in-distribution virtual position. Within this cache, WorldTrace uses the model's own attention to decide which observations to retain verbatim and which redundant ones to merge into compressed summaries, all within one bounded addressable memory bank. We evaluate this ability with LoopBench, a benchmark that tests whether a compressed cache can reconstruct a previously visited scene after a long detour. On LoopBench, WorldTrace improves average DINOv2 recall similarity by 32.6% over a sliding window at the same cache budget, extending visually persistent generation without retraining.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with SVG tree context to assign semantic labels to unlabeled nodes. To reduce redundancy, we introduce depth-adaptive simplification to reduce shape complexity and Tree-Guided Pruning and Merging to eliminate redundant SVG nodes. L1-SAM-Prompting further recovers missing regions to improve recon- struction fidelity and structural completeness. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, we introduce a new evaluation protocol that measures structural quality and semantic part alignment. Experiments demonstrate that Lang-SVG achieves state-of-the-art performance in both rendering fidelity and structural quality. Project website: https://xiliu8006.github.io/Lang-SVG/.

Graphics.title: GraftRay: Physically Based Mesh Insertion into Gaussian Splatting Scenes via Path Tracing
Graphics.summary: We present GraftRay, a unified method for physically consistent insertion of mesh objects into 2D and 3D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS/3DGS) indoor scenes. We lift albedo, roughness, metallic and normals from diffusion-based 2D priors onto the Gaussians by back-projection, model windows and lamps as analytic area emitters, and recover their absolute radiance from ordinary LDR captures with a low-dimensional fit over unit-radiance bases. A path tracer over Gaussians and meshes then produces view-consistent shading, interreflections and soft shadows, which are composited onto the original reconstruction by differential rendering, preserving the untouched background. On synthetic, real and generated scenes, GraftRay outperforms recent insertion and inverse-rendering baselines in image fidelity and shadow accuracy at competitive cost, and users prefer its lighting and shadows over those of the baselines.

Graphics.title: Delaunay-Based Nearest Neighbor Search with Grid-Accelerated Queries and Parallel Construction
Graphics.summary: Nearest-neighbor search is a fundamental primitive in computer graphics, with applications in distance field computation, surface reconstruction, and point cloud registration. In many graphics applications, data points lie on a surface manifold embedded in 3D space, whereas queries are distributed throughout the surrounding volume, a setting in which spatial partitioning structures such as k-d trees and grids can become inefficient. Dynamic-programming-based nearest-neighbor search (DP-NNS) offers an alternative: it traverses a successor DAG that records the history of incremental Delaunay construction and often outperforms spatial partitioning structures. However, its sequential construction is slow, and naive parallelization degrades query performance, limiting its practical adoption. We accelerate both queries and construction in DP-NNS. For queries, we introduce a grid-based initialization strategy that precomputes valid starting points on the successor DAG, shortening search paths while preserving exactness and enabling a twofold speedup. For construction, we analyze how parallel insertion affects query cost and develop a parallel algorithm that preserves logarithmic expected query cost under stated geometric assumptions. Our parallel construction algorithm achieves a 10x speedup over the sequential baseline while maintaining nearly the same query cost. We further reorder query points to improve cache locality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms widely used libraries in nearest-neighbor query performance.

Graphics.title: Instant NuRec: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstruction for Driving Scene Simulation
Graphics.summary: 3D simulation platforms are critical for autonomous driving because they enable end-to-end policy evaluation, thereby reducing development costs and improving safety. In recent years, neural simulation has become predominant, with methods such as NuRec playing a central role; however, these methods remain relatively slow and typically require per-scene tuning. In this work, we present Instant NuRec, a feed-forward neural reconstruction model that turns a short multi-view driving log into a fully simulatable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) world in a single forward pass. The model accepts multi-view input from a calibrated camera rig and emits a layered output consisting of static and dynamic 3DGS layers, a sky cubemap, and per-camera ISP corrections, while providing native support for non-pinhole camera models via 3DGUT. It reconstructs a 10-20-second multi-camera scene in roughly 1.5 seconds and achieves a PSNR on the Waymo Open Dataset that is 2.01 dB above the strongest evaluated baseline. Instant NuRec is deeply integrated into NuRec and is compatible with AlpaSim for closed-loop simulation.

Multimedia.title: PanDent: Toward Comprehensive Tooth-Level Structure-Language Consistency in Dental Radiology
Multimedia.summary: Accurate evaluation of multimodal large language models in dental panoramic radiography is limited by the lack of fine-grained, clinically reliable benchmarks that reflect expert interpretation. This work introduces PanDent, a large-scale benchmark built on expert-validated tooth-level annotations. It comprises 9,554 panoramic radiographs with comprehensive structured findings produced by experienced dentists and further validated by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist. Clinician-guided reports are constructed from these findings using clinician-defined reporting logic, establishing explicit correspondence between structured clinical evidence and free-text descriptions. The dataset supports complementary evaluation of report-level textual agreement and tooth-level clinical consistency, with 9,049 public-source cases for supervised training and an independent 505-case in-house benchmark. Experiments cover proprietary, general-domain open-source, and medical-specific models. Current models generate fluent reports but exhibit substantial errors in fine-grained localization and tooth-level diagnosis. Supervised fine-tuning on PanDent markedly improves report alignment and diagnostic accuracy, bringing predictions closer to expert dental interpretation. These results establish PanDent as a rigorous benchmark and training resource for clinically grounded dental multimodal reasoning. Dataset sample: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Desperado1103/Pandent_Sample; code: https://github.com/HKUDentistry/PanDent. Full data will be released upon publication under source redistribution terms.

Multimedia.title: CineWild: Balancing Art and Robotics for Ethical Wildlife Documentary Filmmaking
Multimedia.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become powerful tools across domains from industry to the arts. In documentary filmmaking, they offer dynamic, otherwise unreachable perspectives, transforming how stories are told. Wildlife documentaries especially benefit, yet UAVs also raise ethical concerns like the risk of disturbing the animals they aim to capture. This paper introduces CineWild, a model predictive control (MPC) formulation for autonomous aerial cinematography that combines robotics, cinematography, and ethics. Building on an MPC solution that jointly controls drone motion and camera focal length, CineWild dynamically adjusts flight paths and camera settings to balance cinematic quality with animal welfare. Key features include adaptive zoom for filming from acoustic and visual safe distances, path-planning that avoids an animal's field of view, and smooth, low-noise maneuvers. CineWild exemplifies interdisciplinary innovation, bridging engineering, visual storytelling, and environmental ethics. We evaluate the formulation in simulation, with ablation studies and a comparison against a cinematographic baseline and a welfare-aware baseline under identical weights, and we demonstrate the perception and camera-actuation pipeline in real-world proof-of-concept trials. We will release the code.

Multimedia.title: PulseGuard: rPPG-Derived Temporal Signals as a Forensic Modality for Talking-Face Deepfake Detection
Multimedia.summary: Talking-face (TF) deepfake generation synthesizes photorealistic facial video from a static source image and an audio signal, producing forgeries that current image-based detectors consistently fail to identify. Unlike face-swap manipulation, TF synthesis has no underlying real video from which to inherit physiological characteristics, motivating remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) as a detection modality for this forgery category. We propose PulseGuard, a detection framework that extracts per-window rPPG waveforms via RhythmFormer and trains a suite of lightweight classifiers to distinguish real from synthesized traces. Evaluated on the TF subset of Celeb-DF++ under a strict subject-independent protocol, where test identities are completely separated from training identities, our 1D ResNet achieves a window-level AUC of 0.826 at EER 25.1% (0.842 pooled to video level, the granularity at which DeepFakesON-Phys is scored) while operating exclusively on the extracted temporal signal, and retains AUC 0.754 on generators withheld entirely from training. We document a controlled reproduction study of DeepFakesON-Phys, the representative prior rPPG detector, demonstrating degradation from AUC 0.999 on legacy face-swap data to 0.576 on the TF subset of Celeb-DF++. We further show that detection difficulty is strongly method-dependent: AUC ranges from 0.937 (Real3DPortrait) to 0.617 (IP-LAP) across the seven TF generators, with the ordering broadly preserved under per-method training. This spread is stable across training regimes rather than reflecting evaluation noise, and constitutes the primary empirical contribution of the work. We report these as empirical baselines and do not establish that the discriminative content is cardiac in origin.
